Every request to the Whatspie API must carry your API token in the Authorization header as a Bearer token. There are no other authentication methods.

Get your API token from the Whatspie dashboard: Developers in the sidebar, or app.whatspie.com/profile?tab=developer. Send the token in the Authorization header of every request. Start using the API. Your token gives access to the devices on your account.

Header Value Description Authorization Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN Your API token. Write Bearer, one space, then the token. Always include Bearer: the MCP server rejects a token without it. Content-Type application/json Needed on requests with a JSON body. Accept application/json The API responds with JSON.

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "chat", "params": { "text": "Hello World!" } }' See Send text message for the request and response fields.

Log in to the Whatspie dashboard at app.whatspie.com. Open Developers in the sidebar, or go to Profile → Developer: app.whatspie.com/profile?tab=developer. Copy your API token from the developer credentials section. Use this token in all API requests.
Store the token securely in your application. Never put the token in client-side code or in logs. Use environment variables in production.

Secure storage: keep the token in environment variables or a secrets manager, not in source code. HTTPS only: always call https://api.whatspie.com, never plain HTTP. Token protection: never expose the token in client-side code or logs. Sending rate: space out your messages. WhatsApp can block numbers that send too much too fast. IP restrictions: call the API only from your own servers, and restrict which of your machines hold the token.

List your devices. This checks the token without sending a message: curl 'https://api.whatspie.com/devices' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' A valid token returns HTTP 200 with the devices on your account (fields trimmed): { "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": [ { "id": 12, "phone": "6281234567890", "status": "ACTIVE", "paired_status": "PAIRED", "webhook_url": null, "created_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z", "updated_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z" } ] } paired_status: "PAIRED" means the device is connected to WhatsApp and can send messages. See Paired status values. An invalid token returns HTTP 403: { "status": 403, "message": "Invalid Authentication Token" }

# Set your API token as an environment variable export WHATSPIE_API_TOKEN="your_actual_token_here" # Use it in a request curl 'https://api.whatspie.com/devices' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $WHATSPIE_API_TOKEN" \ -H 'Accept: application/json'

Authentication errors return HTTP 403 with one of these messages: message Cause Fix Missing Authorization header The request has no Authorization header. Add Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN. Missing token in Authorization header The header has no token after Bearer . Rarely seen: most HTTP clients drop the trailing space, and an empty token then returns Invalid Authentication Token. Check that the token is not empty, and that Bearer is followed by one space. Invalid Authentication Token The token does not match an account, or it is empty. Copy the token again from the dashboard. It may have been revoked or regenerated. Device not found or access denied The device number in the request is not a device on your account. Use a device number listed by GET /devices. Quota or subscription message Your package has no quota left for this request. Check your package and subscription in the dashboard.

Handle this error in your application, for example by alerting an operator instead of retrying.
Check whether one or more phone numbers are registered on WhatsApp before you message them. The check runs through one of your connected devices.
POST https://api.whatspie.com/contacts/check Send your API token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN header. See Authentication.

Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Phone number of the device that runs the check. It must be connected to WhatsApp. phones array of strings Yes Phone numbers to check. At least one.

Format: international format, country code first, without + or a leading zero. Examples: "6281776521626", "1234567890", "447123456789". Avoid: "+6281776521626", "081776521626", "0081776521626". The API does not reject badly formatted numbers. WhatsApp normalises some of them during the check: +6281776521626 and 081776521626 can still come back as true, and phone repeats the number as you sent it. Other formats come back as false. Send the international format, so the number you check is the number you later send to.

curl -L -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/contacts/check' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json; charset=utf-8' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ --data-raw '{ "device": "6281776521626", "phones": [ "6281776521626" ] }'

curl -L -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/contacts/check' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json; charset=utf-8' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ --data-raw '{ "device": "6281776521626", "phones": [ "6281776521626", "6285603051722", "6281234567890", "6289876543210" ] }'

curl -L -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/contacts/check' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json; charset=utf-8' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ --data-raw '{ "device": "6281776521626", "phones": [ "6281776521626", "60123456789", "65123456789", "91987654321", "1234567890", "447123456789" ] }'

{ "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": [ { "phone": "6281776521626", "is_on_whatsapp": false }, { "phone": "6285603051722", "is_on_whatsapp": true }, { "phone": "6281234567890", "is_on_whatsapp": false }, { "phone": "6289876543210", "is_on_whatsapp": false } ] } Field Type Description phone string The number, exactly as you sent it. is_on_whatsapp boolean true if the number has a WhatsApp account. Results come back in the same order as phones.

HTTP status message Cause 400 Invalid request body: ... The body is not valid JSON, or device or phones is missing. 400 Phones array cannot be empty phones is an empty array. 403 Missing Authorization header, Missing token in Authorization header, Invalid Authentication Token Token problem. See Authentication. 403 Device not found or access denied device is not a device on your account. 500 Internal server error The check failed, for example because the device is not connected to WhatsApp. Check the device in Device management. { "status": 403, "message": "Device not found or access denied" }

Number of phones: there is no fixed limit, but numbers are checked one after another, so long lists take longer. Split large lists into smaller batches. Connected device needed: the check uses the device's WhatsApp connection. A disconnected device returns 500.

A device is one WhatsApp number connected to Whatspie. Every message you send goes through a device. These endpoints create, list, update, and delete devices, and return the QR code that connects a device to WhatsApp.

You need a connected device before you can send messages. Follow these steps once per WhatsApp number. Get your API token. See Authentication. Add a device. In the Whatspie dashboard, open Devices in the sidebar and click Add Device. Enter a Device Name, choose a package, and click Create Device. Packages come in Free and Paid plans with different features. Compare them on the pricing page before you choose. Just trying Whatspie? Choose a package marked Free in the Add Device form. You can add a paid device later. Reseller accounts can also use Create device from code. Find the device. It now appears in Devices in the dashboard. From code, call List devices and note the device's id. A new device has paired_status: "UNPAIRED", which means it is not connected to WhatsApp yet. Its phone is still empty (null) until you scan the QR code. Scan the QR code. In Devices, click Connect next to your device to show its QR code. Then scan it with your phone: open WhatsApp, go to Linked devices, and tap Link a device. You have about 20 seconds. Use the API only if your own app must show the QR code, for example to your customers: call Get QR code with that id. Check that it is connected. In Devices, the device's Status column shows that it is connected, and its WhatsApp number appears. From code, call Get device every few seconds until paired_status is PAIRED; its phone field then holds the WhatsApp number. Use that phone number as device when you send messages. Two device identifiers id (a number, for example 5) goes in the URL of device endpoints: /devices/{id}. phone (for example 6281234567890) goes in the device field when you send messages.
https://api.whatspie.com
All device endpoints need your API token: Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN See Authentication.

Operation Method Endpoint Description Create device POST /devices Create a new device on a package. Reseller accounts only (accounts that resell Whatspie devices); others use the dashboard. List devices GET /devices All devices on your account. Get device GET /devices/{id} One device. Get QR code GET /devices/{id}/qr QR code to connect the device to WhatsApp. Update device PUT /devices/{id} Change the phone number, status, or webhook URL. See the warning before using it. Delete device DELETE /devices/{id} Delete a device. {id} is the numeric device id from List devices, not the phone number.

Package codes for Create device. The packages available to your account may differ; check the dashboard. ID Package code Name 1 BETA Beta Tester (Free, one per account) 2 STARTER60K Starter 3 STARTUP240K Startup 4 BUSINESS Business Devices on the BETA package do not receive image, document, or audio files in webhooks.

# Create device with Starter package curl -L -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/devices' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{ "package": "STARTER60K", "name": "Basic Bot" }' # Create device with Business package curl -L -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/devices' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{ "package": "BUSINESS", "name": "Enterprise Bot" }'

Meaningful names: use descriptive names so devices are easy to tell apart. Package selection: choose a package that fits your message volume. Monitoring: watch the connection of critical devices, for example with the device_disconnected webhook.

Secure display: show QR codes only to the person who owns the phone. Anyone who scans it controls the device. Expiry handling: the QR code expires after about 20 seconds; ask for a new one if needed. Auto-refresh: while waiting for a scan, request a new QR code when the old one expires.

Regular checks: during connection, check paired_status with Get device every 3–5 seconds until it is PAIRED. Timeout handling: stop after a reasonable time and show the user a fresh QR code. Error recovery: retry failed QR requests.

See Authentication. 500 Internal server error List Devices could not be read. Try again.

Most accounts can't use this endpoint It is for reseller accounts only. Just getting started? Add your device in the dashboard instead: see Connect your first device. Create a new device on a package plan. The package price is deducted from your balance. POST https://api.whatspie.com/devices Send your API token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN header. curl -L -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/devices' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json; charset=utf-8' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ --data-raw '{ "package": "STARTUP240K", "name": "Customer Service" }'

paired_status Description UNPAIRED Not connected to WhatsApp. Scan the QR code to connect. PAIRED Connected to WhatsApp and ready to send. A device changes back to UNPAIRED when its WhatsApp session ends, for example when it is logged out from the phone.

Get the QR code that connects the device to WhatsApp. On your phone, open WhatsApp, go to Linked devices, tap Link a device, and scan the code. GET https://api.whatspie.com/devices/{id}/qr Send your API token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN header. See Authentication. {id} is the numeric device id from List devices, not the phone number. The phone number goes in the device field when you send messages. Calling this endpoint starts a login session for the device: Whatspie starts a new WhatsApp connection and waits for a phone to scan the code.

response_type must always be url. The name says url, but you do not get a link. You get the QR picture itself, as text. Parameter Type Required Description response_type string Yes Always url. Other values return 400.
curl -L -X GET 'https://api.whatspie.com/devices/5/qr?response_type=url' \ -H 'Accept: application/json; charset=utf-8' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN'

data.qr is the QR picture as text: a base64 data URL that starts with data:image/png;base64,. Show it in an tag: { "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "qr": "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAA..." } } WhatsApp replaces the QR code after about 20 seconds. If it expires before you scan it, call the endpoint again.

HTTP status message Cause 400 Invalid response_type. Only 'url' is supported response_type is missing or not url. 400 Invalid device ID {id} is not a number. 404 Device not found No device with this ID. 403 Access denied The device belongs to another account. 500 Failed to get QR code The QR code could not be generated. Try again. If the device is already connected (paired_status is PAIRED), there is no QR code to return. Check paired_status with Get device before asking for a QR code.

Change a device's phone number, status, or webhook URL. PUT https://api.whatspie.com/devices/{id} Send your API token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN header. See Authentication. {id} is the numeric device id from List devices, not the phone number. The phone number goes in the device field when you send messages. Parameter Type Required Description phone string No Device phone number. status string No Device status. webhook_url string No URL that receives webhooks. Update replaces the device record This endpoint currently saves only the fields in your request and clears the rest of the device record, including fields you did not send. Change the webhook URL and other settings in the Whatspie dashboard instead until this is fixed.

curl -L -X PUT 'https://api.whatspie.com/devices/5' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ --data-raw '{ "phone": "62895383079050", "status": "ACTIVE", "webhook_url": "https://your-webhook-url.com" }'

{ "status": 200, "message": "Device updated successfully", "data": null } Every failure returns 400 with Failed to update device, including a wrong or foreign device ID. A non-numeric {id} returns 400 Invalid device ID.
Add one or more phone numbers to a WhatsApp group. The group's device adds them.
POST https://api.whatspie.com/groups/{id}/members/add Send your API token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN header. See Authentication.
Parameter Type Required Description id integer Yes The group's id from List groups. Not the jid; see Which ID to use.
Parameter Type Required Description participants array of strings Yes Phone numbers to add. At least one.

Format: international format, digits only, without + or a leading zero. Example: "6287830605729", not "087830605729" or "+6287830605729". Why: each number is sent to WhatsApp as <number>@s.whatsapp.net exactly as you wrote it, so +, spaces, or a leading 0 produce an invalid number. WhatsApp: the number must be registered on WhatsApp. Admin permission required The group's device must be a group administrator to add new members.

curl -L -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/groups/2/members/add' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ --data-raw '{ "participants": [ "6287830605729" ] }'

curl -L -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/groups/2/members/add' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ --data-raw '{ "participants": [ "6287830605729", "6281234567890", "6289876543210", "6285544332211" ] }'

curl -L -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/groups/2/members/add' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ --data-raw '{ "participants": [ "6287830605729", "60123456789", "65123456789", "91123456789", "1234567890" ] }'

{ "status": 200, "message": "Members added successfully", "data": { "group_id": 2, "members_added": [ "6287830605729", "6281234567890" ] } } Field Type Description group_id number The group id from the request path. members_added array of strings The participants you sent, returned as-is. Per-number results are not reported members_added repeats your request. It does not say which numbers WhatsApp actually added. A number can still be left out, for example because it is not on WhatsApp or its privacy settings block being added. Check the group in WhatsApp to confirm. A number that is already a member is different: the whole request then fails with 500. See Errors.

HTTP status message Cause 400 Invalid group ID id is not a number, for example a jid. 400 Invalid request body: ... The body is not valid JSON, or participants is missing. 400 Members list cannot be empty participants is an empty array. 403 Missing Authorization header, Missing token in Authorization header, Invalid Authentication Token Token problem. See Authentication. 500 Internal server error Any failure: the group was not found or belongs to another account, the device is not an admin or not connected, a number is already a member, or WhatsApp rejected the request. { "status": 400, "message": "Members list cannot be empty" } { "status": 500, "message": "Internal server error" } The 500 response does not say which of these causes it was. Check that the group id is yours and that the device is connected and an admin.

The examples use this helper: async function addGroupMembers(token, groupId, phoneNumbers) { const response = await fetch(`https://api.whatspie.com/groups/${groupId}/members/add`, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, }, body: JSON.stringify({ participants: phoneNumbers }), }); const result = await response.json(); if (!response.ok) { throw new Error(`${result.status}: ${result.message}`); } return result.data; // { group_id, members_added } }

try { const data = await addGroupMembers('YOUR_API_TOKEN', 2, ['6287830605729', '6281234567890', '6289876543210']); console.log(`✅ Sent ${data.members_added.length} numbers to group ${data.group_id}`); data.members_added.forEach((phone) => console.log(` + ${phone}`)); } catch (error) { console.error('Error adding members:', error.message); }

Clean and validate numbers first, then send them in batches: function validatePhoneNumbers(phoneNumbers) { const validNumbers = []; const invalidNumbers = []; phoneNumbers.forEach((phone) => { const cleanPhone = phone.replace(/[^\d]/g, ''); // digits only if (cleanPhone.length >= 10 && cleanPhone.length <= 15 && !cleanPhone.startsWith('0')) { validNumbers.push(cleanPhone); } else { invalidNumbers.push(phone); } }); return { validNumbers, invalidNumbers }; } async function bulkAddMembers(token, groupId, phoneNumbers, batchSize = 20) { const { validNumbers, invalidNumbers } = validatePhoneNumbers(phoneNumbers); if (invalidNumbers.length > 0) console.warn('Invalid phone numbers detected:', invalidNumbers); if (validNumbers.length === 0) throw new Error('No valid phone numbers provided'); // The API has no batch limit; smaller batches make failures easier to retry const batches = []; for (let i = 0; i < validNumbers.length; i += batchSize) { batches.push(validNumbers.slice(i, i + batchSize)); } const results = []; for (let i = 0; i < batches.length; i++) { const batch = batches[i]; console.log(`Processing batch ${i + 1}/${batches.length} (${batch.length} members)...`); try { await addGroupMembers(token, groupId, batch); results.push({ batch, success: true }); } catch (error) { console.error(`Batch ${i + 1} failed:`, error.message); results.push({ batch, success: false, error: error.message }); } if (i < batches.length - 1) await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000)); } const sent = results.filter((r) => r.success).reduce((sum, r) => sum + r.batch.length, 0); const failed = results.filter((r) => !r.success).reduce((sum, r) => sum + r.batch.length, 0); console.log('\n📊 Bulk Addition Summary:'); console.log(`✅ Sent: ${sent}`); console.log(`❌ In failed batches: ${failed}`); console.log(`📋 Invalid numbers: ${invalidNumbers.length}`); return results; } bulkAddMembers('YOUR_API_TOKEN', 2, [ '6287830605729', '6281234567890', '6289876543210', '+62855-4433-2211', '628-1122-334455', // cleaned to digits 'invalid-number', // rejected '6287766554433', '6281987654321', ]);

async function addMembersFromCSV(token, groupId, csvData) { const lines = csvData.trim().split('\n'); const headers = lines[0].toLowerCase().split(','); const phoneIndex = headers.findIndex((h) => h.includes('phone') || h.includes('number') || h.includes('mobile')); const nameIndex = headers.findIndex((h) => h.includes('name') || h.includes('nama')); if (phoneIndex === -1) throw new Error('No phone number column found in CSV'); const members = []; for (let i = 1; i < lines.length; i++) { const row = lines[i].split(','); const phone = row[phoneIndex]?.trim(); const name = nameIndex !== -1 ? row[nameIndex]?.trim() : ''; if (phone) members.push({ phone, name }); } console.log(`📋 Found ${members.length} members in CSV`); const results = await bulkAddMembers(token, groupId, members.map((m) => m.phone)); const report = { csvMembers: members.length, sent: results.filter((r) => r.success).reduce((sum, r) => sum + r.batch.length, 0), inFailedBatches: results.filter((r) => !r.success).reduce((sum, r) => sum + r.batch.length, 0), details: results, }; console.log('\n📊 CSV Import Report:'); console.log(`📋 CSV records: ${report.csvMembers}`); console.log(`✅ Sent: ${report.sent}`); console.log(`❌ In failed batches: ${report.inFailedBatches}`); return report; } const sampleCSV = `name,phone,email John Doe,6287830605729,john@example.com Jane Smith,6281234567890,jane@example.com Mike Wilson,6289876543210,mike@example.com`; addMembersFromCSV('YOUR_API_TOKEN', 2, sampleCSV);

documents.t: async function addMembersWithProgress(token, groupId, phoneNumbers, onProgress, batchSize = 5) { const batches = []; for (let i = 0; i < phoneNumbers.length; i += batchSize) { batches.push(phoneNumbers.slice(i, i + batchSize)); } const progress = { total: phoneNumbers.length, processed: 0, sent: 0, failed: 0, failedNumbers: [] }; for (let i = 0; i < batches.length; i++) { const batch = batches[i]; onProgress?.({ ...progress, percent: Math.round((i / batches.length) * 100), status: `Batch ${i + 1}/${batches.length}` }); try { await addGroupMembers(token, groupId, batch); progress.sent += batch.length; } catch (error) { progress.failed += batch.length; progress.failedNumbers.push(...batch.map((phone) => ({ phone, error: error.message }))); } progress.processed += batch.length; if (i < batches.length - 1) await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000)); } onProgress?.({ ...progress, percent: 100, status: 'Completed' }); return progress; } const phoneNumbers = Array.from({ length: 50 }, (_, i) => `628${String(i).padStart(9, '0')}`); addMembersWithProgress('YOUR_API_TOKEN', 2, phoneNumbers, (p) => { console.clear(); console.log(`📊 Adding members: ${p.percent}% (${p.status})`); console.log(`Processed: ${p.processed}/${p.total} ✅ ${p.sent} ❌ ${p.failed}`); const filled = Math.round((p.percent / 100) * 30); console.log(`[${'█'.repeat(filled)}${'░'.repeat(30 - filled)}] ${p.percent}%`); });

Group member limit: maximum 1024 members per group. Privacy settings: users can block being added to groups. WhatsApp registration: phone numbers must be registered on WhatsApp. Admin requirement: only group admins can add members.

No batch or rate limit: the API sets no maximum number of participants per request and no rate limit. WhatsApp may still restrict accounts that add many people quickly. No per-number result: the response does not say which numbers were added. Phone format: international format, digits only (no +, 00, or leading 0).

Partial results: WhatsApp may add some numbers and skip others, and the response does not show which. Retries: retry a batch only after a 500, and check the device connection first. Validation: always clean and validate phone numbers before sending. Logging: log the numbers you sent so you can review them later in WhatsApp.

Batch processing: split large member lists into smaller batches. Progress tracking: use progress callbacks for bulk operations. Error reporting: keep a list of numbers in failed batches. User consent: make sure people agree to being added to groups.

The examples use this helper: async function listGroups(token, device) { const url = new URL('https://api.whatspie.com/groups'); if (device) url.searchParams.set('device', device); const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Accept: 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }, }); const body = await res.json(); if (!res.ok) throw new Error(body.message); return body.data; // array of groups }

async function getFilteredGroups(token) { const groups = await listGroups(token); // Unmuted groups const activeGroups = groups.filter((group) => !group.muted); // Groups created on WhatsApp in the last 30 days const thirtyDaysAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000); const recentGroups = groups.filter((group) => new Date(group.group_created_at) > thirtyDaysAgo); console.log(`Active groups (unmuted): ${activeGroups.length}`); activeGroups.forEach((group) => console.log(`- ${group.title} (ID: ${group.id})`)); console.log(`\nRecent groups (last 30 days): ${recentGroups.length}`); recentGroups.forEach((group) => { const createdDate = new Date(group.group_created_at).toLocaleDateString(); console.log(`- ${group.title} (Created: ${createdDate})`); }); return { activeGroups, recentGroups }; }

' (Muted)' : ''}`); }); return recentlyUpdated; }

async function exportGroupsData(token) { const groups = await listGroups(token); if (groups.length === 0) return ''; const exportData = groups.map((group) => ({ ID: group.id, 'Device ID': group.device_id, JID: group.jid, Title: group.title, Description: group.description || 'No description', 'Has Image': group.image_url ? 'Yes' : 'No', Muted: group.muted ? 'Yes' : 'No', Spam: group.spam ? 'Yes' : 'No', 'Group Created': new Date(group.group_created_at).toLocaleDateString(), 'First Synced': new Date(group.created_at).toLocaleDateString(), 'Last Updated': new Date(group.updated_at).toLocaleDateString(), })); // Quote every value and escape quotes, so commas and quotes in titles are safe const toCsv = (value) => `"${String(value).replace(/"/g, '""')}"`; const csvHeaders = Object.keys(exportData[0]).map(toCsv).join(','); const csvRows = exportData.map((row) => Object.values(row).map(toCsv).join(',')); const csvContent = [csvHeaders, ...csvRows].join('\n'); console.log('Groups export ready:'); console.log(csvContent); return csvContent; }

The stored list only changes after a refresh, so a monitor can only detect what a refresh brings in: new groups, changed titles, and groups that are gone. Descriptions are not compared, because a refresh currently clears them. class GroupMonitor { constructor(apiToken, checkInterval = 30000) { // 30 seconds this.apiToken = apiToken; this.checkInterval = checkInterval; this.previousGroups = new Map(); this.isMonitoring = false; } async fetchGroups() { return listGroups(this.apiToken); } detectChanges(currentGroups) { const changes = []; for (const group of currentGroups) { const previous = this.previousGroups.get(group.id); if (!previous) { changes.push({ type: 'new_group', group, message: `New group: ${group.title}` }); continue; } if (group.title !== previous.title) { changes.push({ type: 'name_changed', group, message: `Group name changed: ${previous.title} → ${group.title}`, }); } } for (const [id, previous] of this.previousGroups) { if (!currentGroups.some((g) => g.id === id)) { changes.push({ type: 'group_removed', group: previous, message: `Group no longer listed: ${previous.title}` }); } } return changes; } remember(groups) { this.previousGroups = new Map(groups.map((group) => [group.id, group])); } async startMonitoring(onChanges = null) { this.isMonitoring = true; const initialGroups = await this.fetchGroups(); this.remember(initialGroups); console.log(`Monitoring ${initialGroups.length} groups...`); const monitor = async () => { if (!this.isMonitoring) return; try { const currentGroups = await this.fetchGroups(); const changes = this.detectChanges(currentGroups); if (changes.length > 0) { console.log(`Detected ${changes.length} changes:`); changes.forEach((change) => console.log(`- ${change.message}`)); onChanges?.(changes); } this.remember(currentGroups); } catch (error) { console.error('Error monitoring groups:', error); } setTimeout(monitor, this.checkInterval); }; setTimeout(monitor, this.checkInterval); } stopMonitoring() { this.isMonitoring = false; console.log('Group monitoring stopped'); } } const monitor = new GroupMonitor('YOUR_API_TOKEN', 30000); monitor.startMonitoring((changes) => { changes .filter((change) => change.type === 'new_group') .forEach((change) => console.log(`🔔 ${change.message}`)); }); // Stop monitoring after 10 minutes setTimeout(() => monitor.stopMonitoring(), 600000);

The API does not limit how often you call this endpoint. The list only changes after a refresh, so calling it often returns the same data: Recommended frequency: no more than once every 30 seconds. To see new or changed groups: call Refresh groups first, then list.

documents.t: { "status": 403, "message": "failed to fetch group list from whatspie node: Disconnected" } The device must be connected (paired and online), because the group list is fetched live from its WhatsApp connection.

Whatspie fetches the current group list from the device's live WhatsApp connection. Each group is upserted into the stored list, matched by device and group JID: existing groups are updated in place, newly joined groups are added. Groups you have left on WhatsApp are not removed from the stored list. Title, picture, mute, and spam status are updated from WhatsApp. The stored description is cleared to null on every refresh; see the warning below. Descriptions are cleared A refresh currently sets description to null for every synced group, even if the group has a description on WhatsApp. When to use this Call this endpoint after joining a new group, or periodically if you rely on List groups for up-to-date group data and don't want to wait for the next automatic sync.
List groups: the stored group list (no live fetch) Get group: details of one stored group Send group messages: send messages to groups
Send a message to a WhatsApp group. The message content uses the same params as messages to a phone number.
POST https://api.whatspie.com/groups/{id}/send Send your API token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN header. See Authentication.

Parameter Type Required Description id integer Yes The group's id from List groups, for example 495. Not the jid; see Which ID to use. Group ID Get the group ID from List groups. It is the numeric id of the group.

Parameter Type Required Description type string Yes chat, image, file, or location. See Message types. params object Yes Message content. Same keys as for messages to a phone number. params accepts only these keys: text, caption, fileName, mimetype, location, image, document, video. Any other key is rejected with 400. There is no device or receiver field. The message is sent from the device that the group belongs to: each group id is tied to one device. A device field in the body is ignored. The older format, with the text in a top-level message field and no params, is still accepted for text messages. The API does not check that a chat message has text. A request with neither params.text nor message still returns 200, and the message later ends as ERROR. Always send params.text.

Content type params Details Text chat text Send text Image image image.url, optional caption Send image File file document.url, optional fileName, mimetype, caption Send file Video file video.url, optional mimetype, caption Send video Location location location.degreesLatitude, location.degreesLongitude Send location Text supports WhatsApp formatting (*bold*, _italic_), emoji, and line breaks (\n).

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/groups/495/send' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "type": "chat", "params": { "text": "🎉 *Team Update* 🎉

Great news everyone! Our project milestone has been completed successfully.

✅ All features tested
✅ Documentation updated
✅ Ready for deployment

Thanks for your hard work! 👏" } }'

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/groups/495/send' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "type": "image", "params": { "image": { "url": "https://example.com/team-photo.jpg" }, "caption": "📸 Team lunch today! Great job everyone on completing the sprint goals. 🍽️✨" } }'

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/groups/495/send' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "type": "file", "params": { "document": { "url": "https://example.com/project-report.pdf" }, "fileName": "Project_Report_Q4_2024.pdf", "mimetype": "application/pdf" } }'

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/groups/495/send' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "type": "location", "params": { "location": { "degreesLatitude": -6.2088, "degreesLongitude": 106.8456 } } }'

A successful request returns HTTP 200 with the queued message. The fields are the same as for text messages, with these differences: is_group is true. to_number is the group's JID without @g.us. from_number is the phone number of the group's device. { "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "id": 36259790, "device_id": 5, "from_number": "6281234567890", "to_number": "120363022368688477", "type": "chat", "msg_type": "outgoing", "body": "Team Update: Project milestone completed!", "status": "PENDING", "wa_id": null, "retry": 0, "failed_reason": null, "file_url": null, "file_name": null, "file_caption": null, "file_size": null, "file_mime": null, "params": { "text": "Team Update: Project milestone completed!" }, "is_group": true, "created_at": "2024-12-20T10:30:00Z", "updated_at": "2024-12-20T10:30:00Z" } } The message is sent in the background. Check it later with Get message; see Status values. A group message that WhatsApp accepts is set to SENT.

HTTP status message Cause 400 Invalid group ID id is not a number, for example a jid. 400 Invalid request body: ... The body is not valid JSON, or type is missing. 400 Invalid message type. Must be one of: ... type is not supported, for example text instead of chat. 400 Invalid message params: ... params contains a key that is not allowed. 403 Missing Authorization header, Missing token in Authorization header, Invalid Authentication Token Token problem. See Authentication. 403 Quota or subscription message Your package has no messages left. 500 group not found or access denied: ... No group with this id, or it belongs to another account. 500 Error description Other internal error, for example the message could not be saved. { "status": 500, "message": "group not found or access denied: failed to get group: record not found" } Sending failures, such as a disconnected device or a device that is no longer in the group, do not cause an error response: the API accepts the message first. They show up later as status ERROR with a failed_reason.

The JavaScript examples use this helper: async function sendGroupMessage(token, groupId, type, params) { const res = await fetch(`https://api.whatspie.com/groups/${groupId}/send`, { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json', }, body: JSON.stringify({ type, params }), }); const body = await res.json(); if (!res.ok) throw new Error(body.message); return body; }

Keep group messages clear and structured: const announcement = { type: 'chat', params: { text: '📢 *ANNOUNCEMENT* 📢

' + 'Subject: Weekly Standup
' + '📅 When: Monday 10:00 AM
' + '📍 Where: Conference Room B
' + '⏱️ Duration: 30 minutes

' + 'Please bring your progress updates! 📊', }, }; await sendGroupMessage('YOUR_API_TOKEN', 495, announcement.type, announcement.params);

async function sendToMultipleGroups(token, message, groupIds) { const results = []; for (const groupId of groupIds) { try { const result = await sendGroupMessage(token, groupId, message.type, message.params); results.push({ groupId, success: true, messageId: result.data.id }); } catch (error) { results.push({ groupId, success: false, error: error.message }); } await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000)); // pause between groups } return results; } const update = { type: 'chat', params: { text: "🎉 Company Update: We've reached 10,000 users! Thank you all for your hard work! 🚀" }, }; const results = await sendToMultipleGroups('YOUR_API_TOKEN', update, [495, 496, 497]);

The API sends immediately. To schedule, wait in your own app and send at the right time: function scheduleGroupMessage(token, groupId, message, scheduleTime) { const delay = scheduleTime.getTime() - Date.now(); if (delay <= 0) throw new Error('Schedule time must be in the future'); setTimeout(async () => { try { const result = await sendGroupMessage(token, groupId, message.type, message.params); console.log('Scheduled message queued:', result.data.id); } catch (error) { console.error('Failed to send scheduled message:', error.message); } }, delay); } // Tomorrow at 9 AM const tomorrow9AM = new Date(); tomorrow9AM.setDate(tomorrow9AM.getDate() + 1); tomorrow9AM.setHours(9, 0, 0, 0); scheduleGroupMessage( 'YOUR_API_TOKEN', 495, { type: 'chat', params: { text: '⏰ Reminder: Daily standup in 1 hour! 👥' } }, tomorrow9AM, );

Group membership: the group's device must still be a member of the group. Message size: the same WhatsApp limits as individual messages (16 MB for images, 100 MB for files). Sending rate: WhatsApp may block numbers that send too much to groups. Space out your messages. Admin restrictions: some groups allow only admins to send messages. Delivery tracking: group messages are marked SENT once WhatsApp accepts them; per-member delivery is not tracked. Not supported: mentions, replies to a message, template and list messages to groups.

Before sending, you can check the group with Get group: curl -X GET 'https://api.whatspie.com/groups/495' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' Response: { "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "id": "495", "device_id": "5", "jid": "120363022368688477@g.us", "title": "Project Team", "description": "Development team coordination", "image_url": null, "muted": false, "spam": false, "group_created_at": "2024-11-15T09:00:00Z", "created_at": "2024-11-15T09:05:00Z", "updated_at": "2024-12-20T14:30:00Z" } }

List groups: find a group's id Send text: text message format Send image: image message parameters Send file: file message parameters Send video: video message parameters Send location: location sharing Send template: deprecated template messages Send list: deprecated list messages
Change a group's name, description, or picture. Whatspie applies the change on WhatsApp first, then updates its stored copy of the group.
PUT https://api.whatspie.com/groups/{id} Send your API token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN header. See Authentication.
Parameter Type Required Description id integer Yes The group's id from List groups. Not the jid; see Which ID to use.

All fields are optional; send the ones you want to change. Empty strings are ignored, and a body with no fields returns success without changing anything. Parameter Type Required Description subject string No New group name. The API does not check the length. description string No New group description. The API does not check the length. profile_url string No Public URL of the new group picture. Whatspie downloads it, with a 10-second timeout. The change is made by the device the group belongs to. Admin required The group's device must be a group admin to update group information. Some settings may require creator privileges.

curl -L -X PUT 'https://api.whatspie.com/groups/1' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ --data-raw '{ "subject": "Keluarga Bahagia", "description": "Ini deskripsi keluarga yang bahagia dan harmonis" }'

curl -L -X PUT 'https://api.whatspie.com/groups/1' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ --data-raw '{ "subject": "Keluarga Bahagia", "description": "Ini deskripsi keluarga yang bahagia dan harmonis", "profile_url": "https://wonder-day.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/wonder-day-among-us-21.png" }'

A successful request returns HTTP 200 with the updated group, in the same shape as List groups: { "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "id": "1", "device_id": "5", "jid": "120363022368688477@g.us", "title": "Keluarga Bahagia", "description": "Ini deskripsi keluarga yang bahagia dan harmonis", "image_url": "https://wonder-day.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/wonder-day-among-us-21.png", "muted": false, "spam": false, "group_created_at": "2024-11-15T09:00:00Z", "created_at": "2024-11-15T09:05:00Z", "updated_at": "2024-12-20T15:30:00Z" } } image_url holds the profile_url you sent, not a WhatsApp-hosted copy.

HTTP status message Cause 400 Invalid group ID id is not a number, for example a jid. 400 Invalid request body: ... The body is not valid JSON. 403 Missing Authorization header, Missing token in Authorization header, Invalid Authentication Token Token problem. See Authentication. 500 Internal server error Any failure: the group was not found or belongs to another account, the device is not an admin or not connected, or the picture could not be downloaded. { "status": 500, "message": "Internal server error" } The 500 response does not say which of these causes it was. Check that the group id is yours, that the device is connected and an admin, and that profile_url is a public image URL.

No clearing: an empty description is ignored, so you cannot clear a description with this endpoint. Not supported: group permissions (who can send or edit) and disappearing messages cannot be changed through the API.
Get group: check the stored group details List groups: find a group's id Refresh groups: re-sync the stored list from WhatsApp

The Whatspie API lets your application send and manage WhatsApp messages through WhatsApp numbers you have connected to Whatspie. It is a REST API: you send JSON over HTTPS and get JSON back. With it you can send text, images, files, and locations, work with groups, check whether numbers use WhatsApp, and manage your connected devices. New here? Follow the Quickstart: get a token, connect a WhatsApp number, and send your first message in about 5 minutes. Prefer not to write code? Connect Claude to Whatspie and send WhatsApp messages by asking in plain language. See the MCP Quickstart.
https://api.whatspie.com
Send your API token in the Authorization header of every request: Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN See Authentication for where to find your token.

Every response is a JSON object with the same top-level fields: Field Type Description status number HTTP status code, repeated in the body. message string OK on success, or a description of the error. data object, array, or null The result. null or left out on errors. An error looks like this: { "status": 403, "message": "Invalid Authentication Token" }

Area Pages Messaging Send text, image, file, video, location, reaction; get a message; code examples Groups List, get, refresh, send messages, add members, update Contacts Check whether numbers use WhatsApp Devices Manage devices Webhooks Receive events from Whatspie: Whatspie sends incoming messages and status changes to a URL on your server AI assistants Connect Claude to Whatspie with MCP Deprecated: interactive buttons and lists and template messages. These pages remain for existing integrations.

WhatsApp limits how many messages a number can send. Sending too many messages too quickly can get the number blocked. Group messages: the safe rate depends on group size and how often you send. QR code requests: limited to prevent abuse.
Each guide solves one task. The Whatspie MCP server URL is https://mcp.whatspie.com/mcp; see the Quickstart.

Claude Desktop starts MCP servers as local programs from its config file. To reach the Whatspie MCP server, it uses npx to run mcp-remote, a small bridge that forwards everything to the server: Claude Desktop ──▶ mcp-remote (started by npx) ──HTTPS──▶ Whatspie MCP server npx downloads and starts only the bridge. You need Node.js installed; check with npx -v. Open the Claude Desktop config file. Create it if it does not exist. System Config file macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json Windows, installer version %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json Windows, Microsoft Store version %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\Claude_<id>\LocalCache\Roaming\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json If %APPDATA%\Claude does not exist on Windows, you have the Microsoft Store version. Look in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages for the folder that starts with Claude_. Add the whatspie server. If the file already has an mcpServers object, add the entry inside it. { "mcpServers": { "whatspie": { "command": "npx", "args": [ "-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.whatspie.com/mcp", "--header", "Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER}" ], "env": { "AUTH_HEADER": "Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" } } } } Put the token in env, as shown. On Windows, an argument with a space in it can be split in two, which breaks the header. Keep Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER} exactly as written, with no space after the colon: the bridge fills in ${AUTH_HEADER} from env. Quit Claude Desktop completely: from the system tray on Windows, or with Cmd+Q on macOS. Closing the window is not enough. Then open it again. Open a new chat and open the tools menu. The Whatspie tools are listed there.

Any client that supports MCP over HTTP can connect directly. Add a server of type HTTP with: Setting Value URL https://mcp.whatspie.com/mcp Header name Authorization Header value Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN The header value must start with Bearer and a space. Do not use the client's "Authenticate" or OAuth button: the server uses an API token, not OAuth. Start a new conversation after adding the server.

documents.t: The get_device_qr tool returns the pairing QR code as an image. Use a client that displays images, such as Claude Desktop. Terminal clients such as Claude Code cannot show the image; pair from the Whatspie dashboard instead. Ask: "Show the pairing QR code for device ID 12." On your phone, open WhatsApp, go to Linked devices, tap Link a device, and scan the code. Scan within about 20 seconds. WhatsApp replaces the code after that. If it has expired, ask for it again. Do not ask Claude to redraw or re-encode the QR code. A redrawn code looks correct but does not scan. If the device is already connected, there is no code to scan and the request currently fails with an error. Check the device status first with get_device.

documents.t: Symptom Cause Fix 401 with Missing Whatspie API token The Authorization header is missing, or its value lacks Bearer . Set the value to Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN. Dynamic Client Registration rejected (HTTP 404) or Cannot POST /register Same as above. After a 401, the client tries OAuth, which the server does not support. Fix the header. Do not click "Authenticate". Whatspie API error (403): Invalid Authentication Token The MCP server works, but the Whatspie API rejected the token. Copy the token again from Profile → Developer in the dashboard. It may have been revoked or regenerated. Unexpected error: fetch failed The MCP server could not reach the Whatspie API. Try again. If it keeps happening, contact Whatspie support. 406 Not Acceptable A manual request without the right Accept header. Send Accept: application/json, text/event-stream. Tools do not appear The conversation started before the server was added. Start a new conversation. In Claude Desktop, quit fully and reopen. Claude Desktop: not valid MCP server configurations… skipped The entry uses url, which Claude Desktop does not accept. Use the mcp-remote config in Connect Claude Desktop. Claude Desktop on Windows: spawn npx ENOENT Claude Desktop cannot find npx. Set "command": "cmd" and start args with "/c", "npx". Claude Code: server missing in one folder It was added without --scope user, so it belongs to another folder. Add it again with --scope user. QR code does not scan It expired, or Claude redrew it. See Pair a device with a QR code. Message sent but never arrives The sending device is not connected to WhatsApp. Check the device status in the dashboard and pair it again.
In this tutorial you connect Claude Code or Claude Desktop to the Whatspie MCP server and send a WhatsApp message by asking Claude. It takes about 5 minutes.

Whatspie runs the MCP server for you at https://mcp.whatspie.com/mcp. You connect Claude to it with your Whatspie API token. Nothing to install or keep running on your side, except the small bridge that Claude Desktop needs. You type a request in plain language, such as "send Hi to my colleague". Claude picks the right action (a tool), the MCP server calls the Whatspie API with your API token, and Claude shows you the result. Claude ──MCP──▶ Whatspie MCP server ──▶ Whatspie API MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is the standard that lets Claude use outside tools like this one. Claude Code connects to the server directly. Claude Desktop connects through a small bridge program that it starts with npx.

You need: A Whatspie API token. Find it in the dashboard under Profile → Developer, or at app.whatspie.com/profile?tab=developer. See Authentication. Treat it like a password. A connected device: a WhatsApp number paired with Whatspie. Its paired_status is PAIRED, which means connected to WhatsApp. If you don't have one, follow Connect your first device. One AI app: Claude Code. Check with claude --version. Claude Desktop (download), plus Node.js (download) for the bridge. Check with npx -v. Keep two numbers at hand: your device's phone number (the sender) and a number you can check on a phone (the receiver).

Your token is not stored on the MCP server. Your AI app sends it with every request, in the Authorization header you set up here. Follow the option for the app you use. In both, replace YOUR_API_TOKEN with your token, and keep the word Bearer before the token.

Run this in your terminal (not inside Claude), as one line: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user whatspie https://mcp.whatspie.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" --scope user makes the server available in every folder, not only the current one. Check the connection: claude mcp list You should see a line like this: whatspie: https://mcp.whatspie.com/mcp (HTTP) - ✔ Connected Now start Claude Code in a new terminal with claude. Tools load when a conversation starts, so a conversation that was already open will not see them.

Open the Claude Desktop config file. Create it if it does not exist. If you create it in Notepad, set Save as type to All files, so the file is not saved as claude_desktop_config.json.txt. System Config file Windows %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json Windows, Microsoft Store version %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\Claude_<id>\LocalCache\Roaming\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json. If %APPDATA%\Claude does not exist, you have this version: open %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages in File Explorer and look for the folder whose name starts with Claude_. macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json Quickest way on Windows: run this in PowerShell. Notepad opens the file, and offers to create it if it does not exist. For the Microsoft Store version, put the Store path from the table between the quotes instead. notepad "$env:APPDATA\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json" Put this in the file. If it already has an mcpServers section, add only the whatspie entry inside it, and put a comma between it and the entry before it. The file must stay valid JSON: no missing or extra commas. { "mcpServers": { "whatspie": { "command": "npx", "args": [ "-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.whatspie.com/mcp", "--header", "Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER}" ], "env": { "AUTH_HEADER": "Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" } } } } Keep Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER} exactly as written, with no space after the colon. The bridge fills in ${AUTH_HEADER} from the env section. To check that the file is valid JSON, open it in an editor such as VS Code: it underlines mistakes like a missing comma. Quit Claude Desktop completely (on Windows: right-click its icon in the system tray, then Quit) and open it again. Open a new chat. The Whatspie tools are listed in the tools menu of the chat input. If Claude Desktop shows spawn npx ENOENT, it cannot find npx. Install Node.js and restart Claude Desktop. If the error stays on Windows, replace the whole whatspie entry with this one. It runs npx through cmd: "whatspie": { "command": "cmd", "args": [ "/c", "npx", "-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.whatspie.com/mcp", "--header", "Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER}" ], "env": { "AUTH_HEADER": "Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" } } Didn't work? See Troubleshooting: it lists each error message and its fix.

In a new conversation (Claude Code or Claude Desktop), type: List my WhatsApp devices with their phone numbers and status. Claude asks permission to run the list_devices tool. Approve it. Claude replies with the devices on your account. Find the device whose paired_status is PAIRED (connected) and note its phone number. You use it as the sender in the next step. If the list is empty, or no device is connected, follow Connect your first device first.

Type the following, with your device number as the sender and the number you can check as the receiver. Write numbers in international format without +, for example 6281234567890: Send "Hello from Claude" from device 6281111111111 to 6282222222222. Claude asks permission to run send_text_message. Check the device and receiver in the request, then approve it. Claude replies with the message's ID and status PENDING. This is normal: the message is queued, not failed. Within seconds it changes to SENT or straight to RECEIVED, which means the message reached the phone. Open WhatsApp on the receiving phone. The message "Hello from Claude" arrives from your device's number. Nothing arrived? Check that the device is connected: ask Claude "Show the status of my WhatsApp devices" and check that your device's paired_status is PAIRED, or check it in the dashboard. Ask Claude: "What is the status of the message you just sent?" Claude runs get_message with the message ID from its reply. A status of ERROR comes with a reason; see Status values. You have connected Claude to WhatsApp through Whatspie.
Guides: connect VS Code, pair a device with a QR code, fix connection problems. Reference: every tool and its parameters, and error messages.

The Whatspie MCP server is hosted by Whatspie at https://mcp.whatspie.com/mcp. Every request must include your Whatspie API token, from Profile → Developer in the dashboard: Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN The value must start with Bearer (capital B) followed by one space. A missing header, or a value without Bearer , returns HTTP 401. The server does not store tokens. It forwards the token to the Whatspie API on each request. The server does not support OAuth.

Method and URL Auth Description POST https://mcp.whatspie.com/mcp Yes MCP endpoint, Streamable HTTP transport, stateless (no sessions). Requests must send Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, or the server returns 406. Responses use server-sent events format.

Conventions for all tools: Phone numbers are strings in international format without + or a leading zero, for example 6281234567890. Bare numbers are accepted too. The server does not check or convert numbers: +62… or 08… is passed on to WhatsApp exactly as written. device is the phone number of one of your paired devices. It is the sender. IDs such as group_id, device_id, and id are the numeric IDs used by the Whatspie API, not phone numbers. list_groups and get_group return id as a string, for example "18". The tools accept it as a number or as that string. File URLs must be public, direct links that the Whatspie servers can download. Send tools return the queued message, with its id and status: PENDING. Sending happens in the background; check the status later with get_message.

send_text_message​ Send a text message. Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Sender device number. receiver string Yes Recipient phone number. message string Yes Message text. send_image_message​ Send an image from a URL. JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP, up to 16 MB. Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Sender device number. receiver string Yes Recipient phone number. file_url string Yes Public URL of the image. caption string No Caption shown with the image. send_document_message​ Send a file from a URL, up to 100 MB. Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Sender device number. receiver string Yes Recipient phone number. file_url string Yes Public URL of the file. file_name string Yes File name shown to the recipient, with extension, for example invoice.pdf. mimetype string No MIME type, for example application/pdf. send_reaction​ React to a message with an emoji. Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Sender device number. msisdn string Yes Recipient phone number, or group JID when is_group is true. message_id string Yes WhatsApp message ID (wa_id) to react to. emoji string No Emoji. Default "", which removes the reaction. is_group boolean No true if msisdn is a group. Default false. Returns {"id": "..."}, the WhatsApp ID of the reaction. It does not confirm that the reaction is shown. get_message​ Get one message, including its delivery status. Parameter Type Required Description id number Yes Message ID. list_messages​ List a device's messages, newest first by creation time. Paginated. Each message has msg_type: outgoing for messages you sent, ingoing for messages you received. Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Device number. from string No Only messages from this sender number (exact match), for example 6281234567890. to string No Only messages to this recipient number (exact match). status string No Delivery status in uppercase: PENDING, SENT, RECEIVED, READ, PLAYED, or ERROR. See Status values. Lowercase values match nothing. limit number No Messages fetched from the API before paging. Default 200. page number No Page number, from 1. Default 1. page_size number No Messages per page. Default 20.

list_groups​ List synced groups. Paginated. Parameter Type Required Description device string No Only groups of this device. page number No Page number, from 1. Default 1. page_size number No Groups per page. Default 20. get_group​ Get one group. Parameter Type Required Description group_id number Yes Group ID. refresh_groups​ Re-sync a device's group list from WhatsApp. Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Device number. send_group_message​ Send text, an image, or a file to a group. The message is always sent from the device that owns the group (its device_id in list_groups), so there is no device parameter. Parameter Type Required Description group_id number Yes Group ID. type chat, image, or file No Message type. Default chat. message string For chat Message text. file_url string For image and file Public URL of the media. caption string No Caption, for image. file_name string For file File name with extension. mimetype string No MIME type, for file. The server does not enforce message for chat, file_url for image and file, or file_name for file. Without them the request is still accepted, but the message can end as ERROR; a chat message with no text always does. Always send them. add_group_members​ Add members to a group. The device must be a group admin. Parameter Type Required Description group_id number Yes Group ID. participants string[] Yes Phone numbers to add. Returns {"group_id": 18, "members_added": [...]}. members_added repeats your input, even for numbers that are not on WhatsApp. It does not confirm who joined; check the group in WhatsApp. update_group​ Change a group's details. The device must be a group admin. Parameter Type Required Description group_id number Yes Group ID. subject string No Group name. The server does not check the length. description string No Group description. The server does not check the length. profile_url string No URL of the new group picture.

check_contacts​ Check whether phone numbers are registered on WhatsApp. Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Device number used for the check. phones string[] Yes Phone numbers to check. Returns one entry per number, in the same order: [{"phone": "6281234567890", "is_on_whatsapp": true}].

list_devices​ List the devices on your account. No parameters. get_device​ Get one device. Parameter Type Required Description device_id number Yes Device ID. get_device_qr​ Get the QR code to pair a device. Returns an image. If the device is already paired, the request currently fails with an error. The code expires after about 20 seconds. See Pair a device with a QR code. Parameter Type Required Description device_id number Yes Device ID. create_device​ Create a device. Uses quota and may be billed. Parameter Type Required Description name string Yes Device name. package string Yes Package code from your account. update_device​ Change a device. Can interrupt message delivery. Parameter Type Required Description device_id number Yes Device ID. phone string No New phone number. status string No New status. webhook_url string No New webhook URL. delete_device​ Delete a device permanently. Cannot be undone. Parameter Type Required Description device_id number Yes Device ID. The descriptions of create_device, update_device, and delete_device tell the assistant to confirm with the user before calling them.

The Whatspie API has no page parameters for groups and messages. list_groups and list_messages fetch the list and return one page of it: { "data": [], "page": 2, "page_size": 20, "total": 143, "total_pages": 8 } Field Description data Items on this page. page Current page, from 1. page_size Items per page. total Items fetched in total. total_pages Number of pages. 0 when there are no items. list_groups fetches all groups of the device on every call. list_messages fetches at most limit messages; total counts only those.

Tool errors are returned as MCP tool results with isError: true: Message Meaning Whatspie API error (<status>): <message> The Whatspie API returned an error. <status> is its HTTP status, <message> its error message. Unexpected error: <message> Anything else, for example the MCP server could not reach the Whatspie API (fetch failed). MCP error -32602: Input validation error: ... A required parameter is missing or has the wrong type. The tool did not run. Exceptions: phone-number parameters (device, receiver, msisdn, from, to, phones, participants) accept a number or a string, and IDs (group_id, device_id, id) accept a number or a numeric string. A validation error lists each bad parameter on its own line, after at: MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool send_text_message: Invalid input: expected nonoptional, received undefined at receiver Invalid input: expected string, received undefined at message HTTP errors from the server itself: Status Meaning 401 Missing or malformed Authorization header. 406 Accept header does not include both application/json and text/event-stream.
Get the details and delivery status of one message by its ID. Use it to check a message you sent with any of the send endpoints.
GET https://api.whatspie.com/messages/{id} Send your API token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN header. See Authentication.
Parameter Type Required Description id integer Yes The message ID: data.id in the response of the send request. See Response fields.
curl -X GET 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages/12345' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Accept: application/json'

{ "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "id": 12345, "device_id": 5, "from_number": "6281234567890", "to_number": "6289876543210", "type": "chat", "msg_type": "outgoing", "body": "Hello World!", "status": "SENT", "wa_id": "3EB0C5D3A1B2C4D5E6F7", "retry": 0, "failed_reason": null, "file_url": null, "file_name": null, "file_caption": null, "file_size": null, "file_mime": null, "params": { "text": "Hello World!" }, "is_group": false, "created_at": "2026-06-10T08:30:00Z", "updated_at": "2026-06-10T08:30:02Z" } }

Field Type Description id integer Message ID. device_id integer ID of the WhatsApp device that handled the message. from_number string Sender phone number, international format. to_number string Recipient phone number or group ID. type string Message type, for example chat, image, file, location. msg_type string Direction: outgoing for messages you sent, ingoing (spelled this way in the API) for messages you received. body string Text, caption, or file name of the message. Empty for a location. status string Delivery status. See Status values. wa_id string or null WhatsApp's own message ID. null while the message is PENDING; filled in once WhatsApp accepts it. Used to react to a message. retry integer Number of send retries. failed_reason string or null Why sending failed, when status is ERROR. file_url string or null File URL, when the message was sent with the legacy top-level file_url field. file_name string or null File name, legacy format only. file_caption string or null File caption, legacy format only. file_size integer or null File size in bytes. file_mime string or null MIME type, for example image/jpeg or application/pdf. Legacy format only. params object or null The message parameters, for example text, image.url, document.url, or location. is_group boolean true for a group message, false for a message to a phone number. created_at string When the message was created, ISO 8601. updated_at string When the message last changed, for example its status. ISO 8601.

Status Meaning PENDING Accepted by Whatspie and queued. Not yet handed to WhatsApp. SENT Sent to WhatsApp's servers (one grey tick). RECEIVED Delivered to the recipient's phone (two grey ticks). READ Opened by the recipient (two blue ticks). PLAYED A voice or video message was played. ERROR Sending failed. failed_reason says why. A status only moves forward, from PENDING toward PLAYED, or changes to ERROR. A message can stay at RECEIVED if the recipient has turned off read receipts.

HTTP status message Cause 400 Invalid message ID id is not a number. 404 Message not found or access denied No message with this ID, or it belongs to a device on another account. 403 Missing Authorization header, Missing token in Authorization header, Invalid Authentication Token Token problem. See Authentication. 401 User not authenticated Internal authentication error. A missing or wrong token normally returns 403 first. { "status": 404, "message": "Message not found or access denied" }
Send text, Send image, Send file, Send location: send messages and get their IDs Send reaction: react to a message by its wa_id

Code examples for the send endpoints: helpers, checks before sending, sending many messages, retries, and message templates. For the request and response of each endpoint, see its reference page: text, image, video, file, and location. Start here Copy the Text helper into your project. Send one message with it. Then read Sending many messages and Error handling and retries before you send in bulk. You don't need the rest of this page to get started.
Each example below uses one of these helpers. They send one message and throw an error with status set when the API returns an error.

async function sendTextMessage(token, device, receiver, message) { const res = await fetch('https://api.whatspie.com/messages', { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json', }, body: JSON.stringify({ device, receiver, type: 'chat', params: { text: message } }), }); const body = await res.json(); if (!res.ok) { const error = new Error(body.message); error.status = res.status; throw error; } return body; }

async function sendImageMessage(token, device, receiver, imageUrl, caption) { const params = { image: { url: imageUrl } }; if (caption) params.caption = caption; const res = await fetch('https://api.whatspie.com/messages', { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json', }, body: JSON.stringify({ device, receiver, type: 'image', params }), }); const body = await res.json(); if (!res.ok) { const error = new Error(body.message); error.status = res.status; throw error; } return body; }

async function sendVideoMessage(token, device, receiver, videoUrl, caption, mimetype = 'video/mp4') { const params = { video: { url: videoUrl }, mimetype }; if (caption) params.caption = caption; const res = await fetch('https://api.whatspie.com/messages', { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json', }, body: JSON.stringify({ device, receiver, type: 'file', params }), }); const body = await res.json(); if (!res.ok) { const error = new Error(body.message); error.status = res.status; throw error; } return body; }

async function sendFileMessage(token, device, receiver, fileUrl, fileName, caption) { const params = { document: { url: fileUrl }, fileName }; if (caption) params.caption = caption; const res = await fetch('https://api.whatspie.com/messages', { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json', }, body: JSON.stringify({ device, receiver, type: 'file', params }), }); const body = await res.json(); if (!res.ok) { const error = new Error(body.message); error.status = res.status; throw error; } return body; }

async function sendLocationMessage(token, device, receiver, latitude, longitude) { const res = await fetch('https://api.whatspie.com/messages', { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json', }, body: JSON.stringify({ device, receiver, type: 'location', params: { location: { degreesLatitude: latitude, degreesLongitude: longitude } }, }), }); const body = await res.json(); if (!res.ok) { const error = new Error(body.message); error.status = res.status; throw error; } return body; } // Location pin followed by a text message with its name async function sendNamedLocation(token, device, receiver, latitude, longitude, name) { const location = await sendLocationMessage(token, device, receiver, latitude, longitude); const label = name ? await sendTextMessage(token, device, receiver, name) : null; return { location, label }; }
The API accepts most values without checking them. These checks catch mistakes in your own app before you send.

Check numbers before you send, so typos fail early instead of reaching the API: function isValidPhoneNumber(phoneNumber) { // Country code + number, digits only, no leading zero return /^[1-9]\d{10,14}$/.test(phoneNumber); } function validateWhatspieRequest(device, receiver, message) { if (!isValidPhoneNumber(device)) throw new Error('Invalid device phone number format'); if (!isValidPhoneNumber(receiver)) throw new Error('Invalid receiver phone number format'); if (!message) throw new Error('Message is empty'); return true; } try { validateWhatspieRequest('6281234567890', '6289876543210', 'Hello World!'); await sendTextMessage(token, '6281234567890', '6289876543210', 'Hello World!'); } catch (error) { console.error('Validation failed:', error.message); }

The API does not enforce a maximum length. Long messages are harder to read on a phone, so keep them short. If you want a limit in your own app, check it before sending: function validateMessage(message, maxLength = 4096) { if (message.length > maxLength) { throw new Error(`Message too long. Maximum ${maxLength} characters allowed.`); } return true; }

Check the URL before sending, because the API accepts any URL: function isValidImageUrl(url) { try { const urlObj = new URL(url); if (!['http:', 'https:'].includes(urlObj.protocol)) return false; const imageExtensions = ['.jpg', '.jpeg', '.png', '.gif', '.webp']; return imageExtensions.some((ext) => urlObj.pathname.toLowerCase().endsWith(ext)); } catch { return false; } } async function sendValidatedImage(token, device, receiver, imageUrl, caption) { if (!isValidImageUrl(imageUrl)) throw new Error('Invalid image URL format'); return sendImageMessage(token, device, receiver, imageUrl, caption); }

Check the size before sending, so oversized images fail early: async function getImageSize(url) { try { const response = await fetch(url, { method: 'HEAD' }); const contentLength = response.headers.get('content-length'); return contentLength ? parseInt(contentLength, 10) : null; } catch { return null; } } async function sendOptimizedImage(token, device, receiver, imageUrl, caption) { const size = await getImageSize(imageUrl); const maxSize = 16 * 1024 * 1024; // 16 MB, WhatsApp's image limit if (size && size > maxSize) { throw new Error(`Image too large: ${size} bytes. Maximum allowed: ${maxSize} bytes`); } return sendImageMessage(token, device, receiver, imageUrl, caption); }

Check the URL before sending, because the API accepts any URL: function isValidVideoUrl(url) { try { const urlObj = new URL(url); if (!['http:', 'https:'].includes(urlObj.protocol)) return false; const videoExtensions = ['.mp4', '.mov', '.avi', '.webm', '.mkv', '.flv']; return videoExtensions.some((ext) => urlObj.pathname.toLowerCase().endsWith(ext)); } catch { return false; } } async function sendValidatedVideo(token, device, receiver, videoUrl, caption) { if (!isValidVideoUrl(videoUrl)) throw new Error('Invalid video URL format'); return sendVideoMessage(token, device, receiver, videoUrl, caption); }

async function getVideoSize(url) { try { const response = await fetch(url, { method: 'HEAD' }); const contentLength = response.headers.get('content-length'); return contentLength ? parseInt(contentLength, 10) : null; } catch { return null; } } async function sendOptimizedVideo(token, device, receiver, videoUrl, caption) { const size = await getVideoSize(videoUrl); const maxSize = 64 * 1024 * 1024; // 64 MB, WhatsApp's video limit if (size && size > maxSize) { throw new Error(`Video too large: ${(size / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(2)}MB. Maximum allowed: 64MB`); } if (size) console.log(`Video size: ${(size / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(2)}MB`); return sendVideoMessage(token, device, receiver, videoUrl, caption); }

const VIDEO_RECOMMENDATIONS = { maxSize: 64 * 1024 * 1024, // 64 MB maxDuration: 90, // seconds recommendedFormats: ['mp4', 'mov'], recommendedCodec: 'H.264', recommendedResolution: '1280x720', // 720p }; async function validateVideoForWhatsApp(videoUrl) { const size = await getVideoSize(videoUrl); if (size && size > VIDEO_RECOMMENDATIONS.maxSize) { return { valid: false, message: 'Video exceeds 64MB limit. Please compress or reduce quality.' }; } return { valid: true, message: 'Video meets WhatsApp requirements' }; }

Check the URL before sending, because the API accepts any URL: function validateFileUrl(url) { let pathname; try { const urlObj = new URL(url); if (!['http:', 'https:'].includes(urlObj.protocol)) { throw new Error('File URL must use HTTP or HTTPS protocol'); } pathname = urlObj.pathname; // ignores ?query and #hash } catch (error) { throw new Error(`Invalid file URL: ${error.message}`); } const allowedExtensions = [ 'pdf', 'doc', 'docx', 'xls', 'xlsx', 'ppt', 'pptx', 'txt', 'csv', 'zip', 'rar', '7z', 'tar', 'gz', 'jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'mp3', 'mp4', 'avi', ]; const extension = pathname.split('.').pop().toLowerCase(); if (!allowedExtensions.includes(extension)) { throw new Error(`File type .${extension} is not supported`); } return true; }

function validateCoordinates(latitude, longitude) { const lat = parseFloat(latitude); const lng = parseFloat(longitude); if (isNaN(lat) || lat < -90 || lat > 90) { throw new Error('Invalid latitude. Must be between -90 and 90'); } if (isNaN(lng) || lng < -180 || lng > 180) { throw new Error('Invalid longitude. Must be between -180 and 180'); } return { latitude: lat, longitude: lng }; // numbers, ready for params.location }

Emoji and other Unicode characters are sent as-is: const messages = [ 'Hello! 👋 How are you today?', "Thanks for your order! ✅ We'll process it soon.", '🎉 Congratulations on your achievement!', '❗ Important: Please reply to this message.', '🚨 *URGENT NOTICE* 🚨

Your account will expire in 3 days.

✅ Renew now: https://example.com
💳 Questions? Reply to this message', ]; const token = 'YOUR_API_TOKEN'; const device = '6281234567890'; const receiver = '6289876543210'; for (const [index, msg] of messages.entries()) { try { const result = await sendTextMessage(token, device, receiver, msg); console.log(`Message ${index + 1} queued:`, result.data.id); } catch (error) { console.error(`Message ${index + 1} failed:`, error.message); } await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000)); // pause between messages }

async function sendProductImage(token, device, receiver) { const caption = `🎉 *NEW PRODUCT ALERT* 🎉 _Premium Wireless Headphones_ ✅ Noise Cancellation ✅ 30-hour Battery Life ✅ Fast Charging ✅ Premium Sound Quality ~$299~ *$199* (33% OFF) Use code: *SAVE100* Valid until: December 31st Order now: https://shop.example.com`; return sendImageMessage(token, device, receiver, 'https://example.com/headphones.jpg', caption); }
