// Reverse geocoding: get an address from coordinates, then send it with the pin async function sendLocationWithAddress(token, device, receiver, latitude, longitude) { let name = null; try { const address = await reverseGeocode(latitude, longitude); name = `📍 ${address.name}\n${address.street}, ${address.city}`; } catch { // Address lookup failed: send the pin without a name } return sendNamedLocation(token, device, receiver, latitude, longitude, name); } // Mock reverse geocoding function async function reverseGeocode(lat, lng) { // In a real implementation, use Google Maps, OpenStreetMap, etc. return { name: 'Business Center', street: 'Jl. Sudirman No. 123', city: 'Jakarta', }; }

The location pin and its name const locationResult = await sendNamedLocation(token, device, receiver, latitude, longitude, locationName); // 2. A map image (optional) const mapUrl = generateMapPreview(latitude, longitude); const imageResult = await sendImageMessage(token, device, receiver, mapUrl, '🗺️ Map Preview'); return { location: locationResult, preview: imageResult }; }

documents.t: Format the text you send after the pin: function formatLocationName(name, address = null, category = null) { const categoryEmojis = { restaurant: '🍽️', hotel: '🏨', office: '🏢', hospital: '🏥', school: '🏫', shopping: '🛍️', gas_station: '⛽', bank: '🏦', }; let formattedName = `${categoryEmojis[category] || '📍'} ${name}`; if (address) formattedName += `\n${address}`; return formattedName; } const locationName = formatLocationName('Central Park Mall', 'Jl. Letjen S. Parman, Jakarta Barat', 'shopping'); // "🛍️ Central Park Mall\nJl. Letjen S. Parman, Jakarta Barat"

function calculateDistance(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) { const R = 6371; // Earth's radius in kilometers const dLat = ((lat2 - lat1) * Math.PI) / 180; const dLon = ((lon2 - lon1) * Math.PI) / 180; const a = Math.sin(dLat / 2) * Math.sin(dLat / 2) + Math.cos((lat1 * Math.PI) / 180) * Math.cos((lat2 * Math.PI) / 180) * Math.sin(dLon / 2) * Math.sin(dLon / 2); const c = 2 * Math.atan2(Math.sqrt(a), Math.sqrt(1 - a)); return Math.round(R * c * 100) / 100; // kilometers, 2 decimals } const distance = calculateDistance(-6.2088, 106.8456, -6.1751, 106.865); console.log(`Distance: ${distance} km`);
The API sends one message per request. Space requests out to avoid WhatsApp blocks.

Sending many messages quickly can get your number blocked by WhatsApp. Space your messages out: class MessageSender { constructor(token, device, minIntervalMs = 1000) { this.token = token; this.device = device; this.minIntervalMs = minIntervalMs; this.lastSent = 0; } async sendMessage(receiver, message) { const wait = this.minIntervalMs - (Date.now() - this.lastSent); if (wait > 0) await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, wait)); const result = await sendTextMessage(this.token, this.device, receiver, message); this.lastSent = Date.now(); return result; } }

async function sendImageCatalog(token, device, receiver, products) { const results = []; for (const product of products) { try { const caption = `${product.name}\nPrice: $${product.price}\n${product.description}`; const result = await sendImageMessage(token, device, receiver, product.imageUrl, caption); results.push({ product: product.name, success: true, messageId: result.data.id }); } catch (error) { results.push({ product: product.name, success: false, error: error.message }); } await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000)); // pause between messages } return results; } const products = [ { id: 'p001', name: 'Wireless Headphones', price: 199, description: 'Premium quality with noise cancellation', imageUrl: 'https://example.com/headphones.jpg', }, { id: 'p002', name: 'Smart Watch', price: 299, description: 'Track your fitness and stay connected', imageUrl: 'https://example.com/smartwatch.jpg', }, ]; const results = await sendImageCatalog('YOUR_API_TOKEN', '6281234567890', '6289876543210', products); console.log('Catalog sent:', results);

async function sendVideoToMultipleContacts(token, device, videoUrl, caption, contacts) { const results = []; for (const contact of contacts) { try { const result = await sendVideoMessage(token, device, contact.phone, videoUrl, caption); results.push({ contact: contact.name, success: true, messageId: result.data.id }); } catch (error) { results.push({ contact: contact.name, success: false, error: error.message }); } await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 3000)); // pause between messages } return results; } const contacts = [ { name: 'John Doe', phone: '6289876543210' }, { name: 'Jane Smith', phone: '6281122334455' }, ]; const results = await sendVideoToMultipleContacts( 'YOUR_API_TOKEN', '6281234567890', 'https://example.com/videos/announcement.mp4', '🎉 Important company announcement! Please watch. 🎥', contacts, ); console.log('Videos sent:', results);

async function sendMultipleLocations(token, device, receiver, locations) { const results = []; for (const location of locations) { try { const result = await sendNamedLocation( token, device, receiver, location.latitude, location.longitude, location.name, ); results.push({ location: location.name, success: true, messageId: result.location.data.id }); } catch (error) { results.push({ location: location.name, success: false, error: error.message }); } await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000)); // pause between locations } return results; } const touristSpots = [ { name: '🗿 Monas Jakarta', latitude: -6.1751, longitude: 106.865 }, { name: '🏛️ National Museum', latitude: -6.1717, longitude: 106.8219 }, { name: '🌊 Ancol Beach', latitude: -6.126, longitude: 106.8421 }, ]; await sendMultipleLocations('YOUR_API_TOKEN', '6281234567890', '6289876543210', touristSpots);
Retry only errors that can succeed on a second try. 400 and 403 fail the same way every time.

Retry only errors that can succeed on a second try. Authentication and request errors fail the same way every time: async function sendMessageWithRetry(token, device, receiver, message, maxRetries = 3) { for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++) { try { return await sendTextMessage(token, device, receiver, message); } catch (error) { console.log(`Attempt ${attempt} failed:`, error.message); // 400 and 403 will not succeed on retry if (error.status === 400 || error.status === 403) throw error; if (attempt === maxRetries) throw error; // Exponential backoff: 2 s, 4 s, ... await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2 ** attempt * 1000)); } } } function describeError(error) { switch (error.status) { case 400: return `Bad request: ${error.message}`; case 403: return `Forbidden: ${error.message}. Check your token, device, and quota.`; case 500: return 'Server error: please try again later'; default: return error.status ? `HTTP ${error.status}: ${error.message}` : `Network error: ${error.message}`; } } try { const result = await sendMessageWithRetry( 'YOUR_API_TOKEN', '6281234567890', '6289876543210', 'Hello with error handling!', ); console.log('Message queued:', result.data.id); } catch (error) { console.error('Failed to send message:', describeError(error)); }

Retry only errors that can succeed on a second try: async function sendImageWithRetry(token, device, receiver, imageUrl, caption, maxRetries = 3) { for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++) { try { return await sendImageMessage(token, device, receiver, imageUrl, caption); } catch (error) { // 400 and 403 will not succeed on retry if (error.status === 400 || error.status === 403) throw error; if (attempt === maxRetries) throw error; await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2 ** attempt * 1000)); } } }

Retry only errors that can succeed on a second try: async function sendVideoWithRetry(token, device, receiver, videoUrl, caption, maxRetries = 3) { for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++) { try { return await sendVideoMessage(token, device, receiver, videoUrl, caption); } catch (error) { // 400 and 403 will not succeed on retry if (error.status === 400 || error.status === 403) throw error; if (attempt === maxRetries) throw error; const delay = 2 ** attempt * 1000; console.log(`Retry attempt ${attempt} after ${delay}ms...`); await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delay)); } } }
Images, videos, and files are sent from a public URL. These examples show how to host them.

The API needs a public URL. To send a local file, upload it to your own storage or CDN first, then send its URL: // Pseudo-code: replace uploadImageToCDN with your storage provider's upload call async function uploadImageToCDN(filePath) { const formData = new FormData(); formData.append('file', new Blob([await fs.promises.readFile(filePath)])); const response = await fetch('https://your-cdn.com/upload', { method: 'POST', body: formData }); const { url } = await response.json(); return url; // public URL } async function sendLocalImage(token, device, receiver, localFilePath, caption) { const publicUrl = await uploadImageToCDN(localFilePath); return sendImageMessage(token, device, receiver, publicUrl, caption); }

Send a document or any other file from a public URL to a phone number. The recipient receives it as a WhatsApp document they can open or save.
POST https://api.whatspie.com/messages Send your API token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN header. See Authentication.

Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Phone number of your sending device: the phone field from List devices, not the numeric device id. receiver string Yes Recipient's phone number. Up to 35 characters. type string Yes file. params object Yes Message content. params.document.url string Yes Direct, public URL of the file. params.fileName string No, recommended File name shown to the recipient, with extension, for example invoice.pdf. Without it, the recipient may see an unclear name. params.mimetype string No, recommended MIME type, for example application/pdf. Helps WhatsApp show the right icon and open the file with the right app. params.caption string No Text shown with the file. Write phone numbers in international format without +. See Phone number format. params accepts only these keys: text, caption, fileName, mimetype, location, image, document, video. Any other key is rejected with 400.

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "file", "params": { "document": { "url": "https://example.com/documents/report.pdf" }, "fileName": "Monthly_Sales_Report_Q4_2024.pdf", "mimetype": "application/pdf" } }' In these examples, 6281234567890 is your device (the phone from List devices) and 6289876543210 is the receiver. Replace both with your own numbers.

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "file", "params": { "document": { "url": "https://cdn.example.com/files/presentation.pptx" }, "fileName": "Product_Launch_Presentation_Q1.pptx", "mimetype": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation", "caption": "Slides for Monday'\''s launch meeting" } }'

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "file", "file_url": "https://docs.example.com/api/documentation.pdf", "message": "📚 API Documentation v2.1\n\nLatest version with new endpoints and examples." }' The recipient gets documentation.pdf with the text from message as its caption.

The API does not download or check the file when it accepts your request. WhatsApp applies its own limits when the file is delivered. Commonly sent formats: Category Formats Documents PDF (.pdf), Word (.doc, .docx), Excel (.xls, .xlsx), PowerPoint (.ppt, .pptx), text (.txt) Archives ZIP (.zip), RAR (.rar), 7-Zip (.7z), TAR (.tar, .tar.gz) Development JavaScript (.js, .jsx), Python (.py), Java (.java), C/C++ (.c, .cpp, .h), HTML/CSS (.html, .css) Media Audio (.mp3, .wav, .ogg), video (.mp4, .avi, .mov), images (.jpg, .png, .gif), eBooks (.epub, .mobi) Media files sent this way arrive as documents, not as photos or playable videos. To send a photo, use Send image. Maximum file size: 100 MB.

A successful request returns HTTP 200 with the queued message. The fields are the same as for text messages. For a file sent with params: body holds the caption, or the file name if there is no caption. params holds the document URL, file name, MIME type, and caption. file_url, file_name, and file_mime are null. { "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "id": 36259784, "device_id": 12, "from_number": "6281234567890", "to_number": "6289876543210", "type": "file", "msg_type": "outgoing", "body": "Monthly_Sales_Report_Q4_2024.pdf", "status": "PENDING", "wa_id": null, "retry": 0, "failed_reason": null, "file_url": null, "file_name": null, "file_caption": null, "file_size": null, "file_mime": null, "params": { "fileName": "Monthly_Sales_Report_Q4_2024.pdf", "mimetype": "application/pdf", "document": { "url": "https://example.com/documents/report.pdf" } }, "is_group": false, "created_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z", "updated_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z" } } With the legacy format, body holds message, file_url holds the URL, file_name holds the name taken from the URL, file_mime holds the guessed MIME type, and file_caption holds file_caption if you sent it.

HTTP status message Cause 400 Invalid message params: ... params contains a key that is not allowed, or document is not an object with only url. 400 File URL is required for file type Legacy format without file_url, or a request with neither params nor file_url. 400 File name is required in message field for file type Legacy format without message. Despite the wording, message is used as the caption. 400 Invalid request body: ... The body is not valid JSON, or device, receiver, or type is missing. 403 Missing Authorization header, Missing token in Authorization header, Invalid Authentication Token Token problem. See Authentication. 403 Device not found or access denied device is not a device on your account. 403 Quota or subscription message Your package has no messages left. 500 Error description Internal error, for example the message could not be saved. Try again later. Problems with the file itself, such as a dead link, a private URL, or a file that is too large, do not cause an error response because the API accepts the request first and sends it in the background. The same goes for sending failures, such as a disconnected device or a number that is not on WhatsApp. They show up later as status ERROR with a failed_reason. Check them with Get message; see Status values.

The older format, without params, is still accepted for backward compatibility. It behaves differently from what the field names suggest: Parameter Type Required Description file_url string Yes Direct, public URL of the file. message string Yes Used as the caption, not as the file name. file_caption string No If set, used as the caption instead of message. In this format the file name is taken from the end of the URL (.../report.pdf → report.pdf) and the MIME type is guessed from the file extension. To choose the file name yourself, use params.
JavaScript helpers, validation, batch sending, retries, and use cases for file messages are in the Messaging guide.

File size: up to 100 MB per file (WhatsApp limit). File URL: must be public and reachable over HTTP or HTTPS. The API does not check it; see Errors. File types: WhatsApp may refuse some file types. Large files: take longer to deliver. Retention: files may be cached temporarily for delivery.
Send image: send photos that display inline Send text: plain text messages Get message: check a message's delivery status

Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Phone number of your sending device: the phone field from List devices, not the numeric device id. receiver string Yes Recipient's phone number. _Premium Quality Headphones_

*Special Price: $199*
~Original: $299~" } }'

The API does not download or check the image when it accepts your request. WhatsApp applies its own limits when the image is delivered: Format Notes JPEG / JPG Most compatible format. PNG Supports transparency. GIF Animated images. WebP Modern format. Maximum file size: 16 MB. Recommended dimensions: up to 1600 × 1600 pixels. Accessibility: the URL must be public and point directly to the image file, not to a web page or a login-protected link. Processing: WhatsApp may compress the image when it is delivered.

A successful request returns HTTP 200 with the queued message. The fields are the same as for text messages. For an image sent with params: body holds the caption, or an empty string without one. params holds the image URL and caption. file_url, file_name, and file_mime are null. They are filled only when you use the older top-level file_url format. { "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "id": 36259783, "device_id": 12, "from_number": "6281234567890", "to_number": "6289876543210", "type": "image", "msg_type": "outgoing", "body": "Check out this amazing photo! 📸✨", "status": "PENDING", "wa_id": null, "retry": 0, "failed_reason": null, "file_url": null, "file_name": null, "file_caption": null, "file_size": null, "file_mime": null, "params": { "caption": "Check out this amazing photo! 📸✨", "image": { "url": "https://example.com/images/photo.jpg" } }, "is_group": false, "created_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z", "updated_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z" } }

{ "status": 400, "message": "Invalid message params: unknown parameter 'viewOnce'. Allowed parameters: text, caption, fileName, mimetype, location, image, document" } Note: this error message leaves out video. All allowed keys are listed under Request. HTTP status message Cause 400 Invalid message params: ... params contains a key that is not allowed, or image is not an object with only url. 400 File URL is required for image type The request has neither params nor a legacy file_url field. 400 Invalid request body: ... The older format, with the image URL in a top-level file_url field and the caption in a top-level message field, is still accepted for backward compatibility. New integrations should use params.
JavaScript helpers, validation, batch sending, retries, and use cases for image messages are in the Messaging guide.

File size: up to 16 MB per image (WhatsApp limit). Formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP (WhatsApp limit). URL: must be public and direct. The API does not check it; see Errors. Sending rate: space out your messages to avoid WhatsApp blocks.

Deprecated: not available in the current API Interactive list messages cannot be sent through the current Whatspie API. A list request is rejected with 400. This page documents the former request format for existing integrations that need to migrate. To offer choices today, send a text message with numbered options and ask the recipient to reply with a number.

POST /messages still accepts type: "list", but the list content cannot pass validation: With params: params accepts only text, caption, fileName, mimetype, location, image, document, and video. The list keys title, footer, buttonText, and sections are rejected with 400 Invalid message params: unknown parameter .... Without params: the request is rejected with 400 Params are required for message type: list. With params that contain only allowed keys, for example {"text": "..."}, the message is accepted but delivered as a plain text message, not as a list. The same rules apply to group messages. WhatsApp has also limited interactive list and button messages for unofficial clients, so they may not display even where they could be sent.

This is the format the earlier API accepted. The current API rejects it. POST https://api.whatspie.com/messages Parameter Type Description device string Your sending device number. receiver string Recipient's phone number. type string list. params.title string List title. params.text string List description text. params.footer string Footer text. Optional. params.buttonText string Text on the button that opens the list. params.sections array Sections, each with a title and rows. params.sections[].rows[].title string Row title. params.sections[].rows[].rowId string Unique ID of the row. params.sections[].rows[].description string Row description. Optional.

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "list", "params": { "title": "Tony'\''s Pizza Menu", "text": "Choose from our menu.", "footer": "Free delivery on orders over $25", "buttonText": "View Menu", "sections": [ { "title": "Pizzas", "rows": [ { "title": "Margherita Pizza", "rowId": "pizza_margherita", "description": "Tomato, mozzarella, basil - $12" }, { "title": "Pepperoni Pizza", "rowId": "pizza_pepperoni", "description": "Pepperoni, mozzarella - $15" } ] }, { "title": "Salads", "rows": [ { "title": "Caesar Salad", "rowId": "salad_caesar", "description": "Lettuce, parmesan, croutons - $8" } ] } ] } }'

{ "status": 400, "message": "Invalid message params: unknown parameter 'title'. Allowed parameters: text, caption, fileName, mimetype, location, image, document" } The rejected key named in the message can be any of the list keys.

These were WhatsApp's limits for list messages. They are kept for reference only. Up to 10 sections per list and 10 rows per section, 100 items in total. List title: up to 24 characters. Description text: up to 1024 characters. Button text: up to 20 characters. Row title: up to 24 characters. Row description: up to 72 characters.

Send the options as numbered text: curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "chat", "params": { "text": "*Tony'''s Pizza Menu*

1. Margherita Pizza - $12
2. Pepperoni Pizza - $15
3. Caesar Salad - $8

Reply with a number to order." } }'

Send a location pin to a phone number. The recipient sees a map preview and can open it in their map app. A location message carries only the coordinates. It has no name or address. To tell the recipient what the place is, send the name as a separate text message; see Location with a name.
POST https://api.whatspie.com/messages Send your API token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN header. See Authentication.

Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Phone number of your sending device: the phone field from List devices, not the numeric device id. receiver string Yes Recipient's phone number. Up to 35 characters. type string Yes location. params object Yes Message content. params.location.degreesLatitude number Yes Latitude, -90 to 90. params.location.degreesLongitude number Yes Longitude, -180 to 180. Write phone numbers in international format without +. See Phone number format. params.location accepts only degreesLatitude and degreesLongitude. Other keys, such as name or address, are rejected with 400. Send coordinates as JSON numbers, not strings. Location messages have no legacy format: a request without params is rejected.

Coordinates use WGS84, the same system as GPS. Latitude Longitude Range -90 to +90 -180 to +180 Positive values North East Negative values South West Example (San Francisco) 37.7749 -122.4194 Example (Jakarta) -6.2088 106.8456 The API does not check the range. Validate coordinates yourself; see Coordinate validation.

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "location", "params": { "location": { "degreesLatitude": -6.2088, "degreesLongitude": 106.8456 } } }' In these examples, 6281234567890 is your device (the phone from List devices) and 6289876543210 is the receiver. Replace both with your own numbers.

Send the location, then send the name as a text message right after it: # 1. The location pin curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "location", "params": { "location": { "degreesLatitude": -6.1751, "degreesLongitude": 106.8650 } } }' # 2. The name, as a text message curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "chat", "params": { "text": "📍 Monas - National Monument Jakarta" } }'

# 1. The office location curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "location", "params": { "location": { "degreesLatitude": 37.7749, "degreesLongitude": -122.4194 } } }' # 2. The office name and address curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "chat", "params": { "text": "🏢 Our Office - 123 Business St, San Francisco, CA" } }'

A successful request returns HTTP 200 with the queued message. The fields are the same as for text messages. For a location, body is an empty string and params.location holds the coordinates: { "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "id": 36259785, "device_id": 12, "from_number": "6281234567890", "to_number": "6289876543210", "type": "location", "msg_type": "outgoing", "body": "", "status": "PENDING", "wa_id": null, "retry": 0, "failed_reason": null, "file_url": null, "file_name": null, "file_caption": null, "file_size": null, "file_mime": null, "params": { "location": { "degreesLatitude": -6.2088, "degreesLongitude": 106.8456 } }, "is_group": false, "created_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z", "updated_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z" } }

{ "status": 400, "message": "Invalid message params: unknown location parameter 'name'. Allowed location parameters: degreesLatitude, degreesLongitude" } HTTP status message Cause 400 Invalid message params: unknown location parameter ... params.location contains a key other than degreesLatitude and degreesLongitude. 400 Invalid message params: params validation failed: ... A coordinate is not a number, for example a string. 400 Invalid message params: location parameter must be an object ... params.location is not an object. 400 Params are required for message type: location The request has no params. 400 Invalid request body: ... The body is not valid JSON, or device, receiver, or type is missing. 403 Missing Authorization header, Missing token in Authorization header, Invalid Authentication Token Token problem. See Authentication. 403 Device not found or access denied device is not a device on your account. 403 Quota or subscription message Your package has no messages left. 500 Error description Internal error, for example the message could not be saved. Try again later. Coordinates outside the valid range are not rejected. Check them before sending. Sending failures, such as a disconnected device or a number that is not on WhatsApp, do not cause an error response either: the API accepts the message first and sends it in the background. They show up later as status ERROR with a failed_reason. Check them with Get message; see Status values.
JavaScript helpers, validation, batch sending, retries, and use cases for location messages are in the Messaging guide.

No name or address: a location message carries only coordinates. Send the name as a separate text message. Coordinate precision: up to 6 decimal places is enough for accuracy. Map providers: how the location displays depends on the recipient's map app. Real-time tracking: static location only, no live location. Offline access: recipients need internet to view map details.
Send text: send the place name or directions Send image: send map screenshots Get message: check a message's delivery status
For address lookup and map images, consider: Google Maps API: address lookup and static maps OpenStreetMap: open source mapping Mapbox: custom map styling HERE Maps: enterprise mapping
Add an emoji reaction to a message in a personal chat or a group, or remove one.
POST https://api.whatspie.com/messages/reaction Send your API token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN header. See Authentication.

Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Phone number of your sending device: the phone field from List devices, not the numeric device id. msisdn string Yes The chat the message is in: the other person's phone number for a personal chat, or the group's jid when is_group is true. message_id string Yes The WhatsApp message ID (wa_id) of the message to react to. emoji string No The emoji, for example 👍. An empty string "" removes your reaction. is_group boolean No true for a message in a group. Default false. For groups, use the jid field from List groups, for example 120363022368688477@g.us, not the numeric id. The @g.us suffix is added if you leave it out. Finding the message_id The message_id is the message's wa_id. Messages you sent: wa_id is null right after sending. It is filled in once WhatsApp accepts the message. Read it with Get message. Messages you received: wa_id comes with the incoming message, for example through webhooks. There is no endpoint to search messages yet, so keep the IDs in your own records. Current limitation Reactions are currently sent as reactions to a message you received in a personal chat. A reaction to a message you sent yourself, or to another member's message in a group, may not appear in WhatsApp, even though the API returns 200.

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages/reaction' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "msisdn": "6289876543210", "message_id": "3EB0C767D26A1D8B12A3", "emoji": "👍" }'

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages/reaction' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "msisdn": "120363022368688477@g.us", "message_id": "3EB0C767D26A1D8B12A3", "emoji": "🎉", "is_group": true }'

Send an empty emoji to remove a reaction you sent earlier: curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages/reaction' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "msisdn": "6289876543210", "message_id": "3EB0C767D26A1D8B12A3", "emoji": "" }'

{ "status": 200, "message": "Reaction sent", "data": { "id": "3EB0A1F2C3D4E5F60718" } } Field Type Description id string WhatsApp ID of the reaction itself. This is a new ID, not the message_id you reacted to. Reactions are sent straight to WhatsApp. They are not stored as messages in Whatspie, so you cannot look them up with Get message.
{ "status": 400, "message": "Invalid request body: Key: 'MSISDN' Error:Field validation for 'MSISDN' failed on the 'required' tag" }
{ "status": 403, "message": "Device not found or access denied" }

HTTP status message Cause 400 Invalid request body: ... The body is not valid JSON, or device, msisdn, or message_id is missing. 403 Missing Authorization header, Missing token in Authorization header, Invalid Authentication Token Token problem. See Authentication. 403 Device not found or access denied device is not a device on your account. 403 failed to send reaction via whatspie node: ... containing Disconnected or Connection issue The device is not connected to WhatsApp, or Whatspie could not reach it. Reconnect the device. 500 failed to send reaction via whatspie node: ... Any other sending error. Try again later.

Fire-and-forget: the API returns success once the reaction is sent to WhatsApp, even if message_id is wrong or the message no longer exists. WhatsApp ignores reactions that do not match a message, so there is no way to confirm that a reaction attached. Emoji validation: any string is accepted as emoji, but only a single valid emoji shows as a reaction in WhatsApp. Use an empty string to remove a reaction. Group reactions: set is_group to true and pass the group's jid from List groups as msisdn.
Get message: read the wa_id of a message you sent Send text: send a message List groups: find a group's jid for is_group: true

Deprecated: not available in the current API Template messages with buttons cannot be sent through the current Whatspie API. A template request is rejected with 400. This page documents the former request format for existing integrations that need to migrate. To offer actions today, send a text message with the links, phone number, or numbered options written in the text.

POST /messages still accepts type: "template", but the template content cannot pass validation: With params: params accepts only text, caption, fileName, mimetype, location, image, document, and video. The template keys footer, templateButtons, and buttons are rejected with 400 Invalid message params: unknown parameter .... Without params: the request is rejected with 400 Params are required for message type: template. With params that contain only allowed keys, for example {"text": "..."}, the message is accepted but delivered as a plain text message without buttons. The same rules apply to group messages. WhatsApp has also limited button messages for unofficial clients, so they may not display even where they could be sent.

This is the format the earlier API accepted. The current API rejects it. POST https://api.whatspie.com/messages Parameter Type Description device string Your sending device number. receiver string Recipient's phone number. type string template. params.text string Main message text. params.footer string Footer text. Optional. params.templateButtons array Action buttons: URL, call, or quick reply. Optional. params.buttons array Simple reply buttons. Optional.

Button Key in templateButtons[] Fields Action URL urlButton displayText, url Opens a link. Call callButton displayText, phoneNumber Starts a phone call. Quick reply quickReplyButton displayText Sends a reply. Each templateButtons[] entry also had an index (1, 2, 3). Simple reply buttons in buttons[] had buttonId, buttonText.displayText, and type: 1.

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "template", "params": { "text": "Welcome to Whatspie! Thanks for choosing our service.", "footer": "Powered by Whatspie API", "templateButtons": [ { "index": 1, "urlButton": { "displayText": "Visit Whatspie", "url": "https://whatspie.com" } }, { "index": 2, "callButton": { "displayText": "Call Support", "phoneNumber": "+6285603051722" } }, { "index": 3, "quickReplyButton": { "displayText": "Quick Help" } } ] } }'

{ "status": 400, "message": "Invalid message params: unknown parameter 'footer'. Allowed parameters: text, caption, fileName, mimetype, location, image, document" } The rejected key named in the message can be any of the template keys.

These were WhatsApp's limits for button messages. They are kept for reference only. Up to 3 template buttons or 10 reply buttons per message. Main text: up to 1024 characters. Footer: up to 60 characters. Button text: up to about 20 characters. URLs had to be valid; call-button numbers in international format.

Put the actions in the text. WhatsApp turns links and phone numbers into tappable links: curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "chat", "params": { "text": "Welcome to Whatspie! Thanks for choosing our service.

Visit: https://whatspie.com
Support: +6285603051722

Reply *HELP* for quick help." } }'
Send text: plain text messages Send list (deprecated): list messages, also unavailable Send image: images with captions Get message: check a message's delivery status
Send a text message from one of your devices to a phone number. The text supports WhatsApp formatting and emoji.
POST https://api.whatspie.com/messages Send your API token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN header. See Authentication.

Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Phone number of your sending device: the phone field from List devices, not the numeric device id. receiver string Yes Recipient's phone number. Up to 35 characters. type string Yes chat for a text message. params object Yes Message content. params.text string Yes The text to send. Supports WhatsApp formatting. Write phone numbers in international format without +. See Phone number format. params accepts only these keys: text, caption, fileName, mimetype, location, image, document, video. Any other key is rejected.

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "chat", "params": { "text": "*Bold* _italic_ ~strikethrough~ ```monospace```\n\nNew paragraph with emoji 🎉" } }' In these examples, 6281234567890 is your device (the phone from List devices) and 6289876543210 is the receiver. Replace both with your own numbers.

A successful request returns HTTP 200 with the queued message: { "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "id": 36259782, "device_id": 12, "from_number": "6281234567890", "to_number": "6289876543210", "type": "chat", "msg_type": "outgoing", "body": "Hello World!", "status": "PENDING", "wa_id": null, "retry": 0, "failed_reason": null, "file_url": null, "file_name": null, "file_caption": null, "file_size": null, "file_mime": null, "params": { "text": "Hello World!" }, "is_group": false, "created_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z", "updated_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z" } } 200 OK does not mean delivered The API queues the message and sends it in the background. If the device is disconnected or the number is not on WhatsApp, you still get 200. The status changes to ERROR later. Check it with Get message.

Field Type Description id number Message ID. Use it with Get message to check the message later. device_id number ID of the sending device. from_number string Sender device number. to_number string Recipient's phone number. type string chat. msg_type string outgoing for messages you send. body string The text that was sent. status string Delivery status. PENDING right after the request: the message is queued, not yet delivered. It changes as delivery progresses; see Status values. wa_id string or null WhatsApp's own message ID. null while the message is PENDING; filled in after WhatsApp accepts it. retry number Number of send retries. failed_reason string or null Why sending failed, if it did. file_url, file_name, file_caption, file_size, file_mime null Not used for text messages. params object Stored message parameters: { "text": "..." }. is_group boolean false for messages to a phone number. created_at, updated_at string Timestamps, ISO 8601.

Errors return the HTTP status in status and a description in message: { "status": 400, "message": "Invalid message params: unknown parameter 'body'. Allowed parameters: text, caption, fileName, mimetype, location, image, document" } Note: this error message leaves out video. All allowed keys are listed under Request. HTTP status message Cause 400 Invalid message params: ... params contains a key that is not allowed, or a nested value has the wrong shape. 400 Message text is required for chat type The request has neither params nor a legacy message field. 400 Invalid request body: ... The body is not valid JSON, or device, receiver, or type is missing. 400 Invalid message type. Must be one of: ... type is not a supported message type. 403 Missing Authorization header No Authorization header. 403 Missing token in Authorization header The header has no token after Bearer . 403 Invalid Authentication Token The token is wrong or revoked. 403 Device not found or access denied device is not a device on your account. 403 Quota or subscription message Your package has no messages left. 500 Error description Internal error, for example the message could not be saved. Try again later. Sending failures, such as a disconnected device or a number that is not on WhatsApp, do not cause an error response either: the API accepts the message first and sends it in the background. They show up later as status ERROR with a failed_reason. Check them with Get message; see Status values.

Write device and receiver in international format: country code followed by the number, without +, spaces, or hyphens. Country Format Example USA 1XXXXXXXXXX 11234567890 UK 44XXXXXXXXXX 441234567890 India 91XXXXXXXXXX 911234567890 Indonesia 62XXXXXXXXXXX 6281234567890 Brazil 55XXXXXXXXXXX 5511987654321 Germany 49XXXXXXXXXX 491234567890 Invalid formats: +6281234567890: contains + 081234567890: missing country code 6281-234-567-890: contains hyphens 62 81234567890: contains spaces

WhatsApp formatting works in params.text: Style Syntax Example Bold *text* *Order confirmed* Italic _text_ _optional_ Strikethrough ~text~ ~old price~ Monospace ```text``` ```ABC-123``` Use \n in JSON for a line break. Emoji and other Unicode characters are sent as-is.

# Bold text curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "chat", "params": { "text": "This is *bold text* in WhatsApp" } }' # Mixed formatting curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "chat", "params": { "text": "*Bold* _italic_ ~strike~ text combined!" } }'
The older format, with the text in a top-level message field and no params, is still accepted for backward compatibility. New integrations should use params.
JavaScript helpers, validation, batch sending, retries, and use cases for text messages are in the Messaging guide.

Message length: the API sets no limit. Keep messages readable on a phone. Sending rate: about 1–2 messages per second is a common safe rate to avoid temporary blocks. Recipients: must have an active WhatsApp account. Use Check contacts to verify numbers first. Sending device: must be connected to WhatsApp. A disconnected device cannot deliver messages. See Device management. WhatsApp policies: follow WhatsApp's business messaging policies and terms. International numbers: always include the country code.

Send image: images with captions Send file: documents and other files Send location: location coordinates Get message: check a message's delivery status Device management: check that your device is connected Authentication: API tokens

Send a video from a public URL to a phone number, with an optional caption. The recipient can play it inline in WhatsApp. Videos use type: "file" with a params.video object. In Whatspie, type is a label for the message; what WhatsApp receives is decided by params. With params.video the recipient gets a playable video, while params.document (see Send file) would deliver the same file as a document.
POST https://api.whatspie.com/messages Send your API token in the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN header. See Authentication.

Parameter Type Required Description device string Yes Phone number of your sending device: the phone field from List devices, not the numeric device id. receiver string Yes Recipient's phone number. Up to 35 characters. type string Yes file. There is no video type; it is rejected with 400. params object Yes Message content. params.video.url string Yes Direct, public URL of the video file. params.mimetype string No, recommended Video MIME type, for example video/mp4. See Common video MIME types. params.caption string No Caption shown under the video. Supports WhatsApp formatting. Write phone numbers in international format without +. See Phone number format. params accepts only these keys: text, caption, fileName, mimetype, location, image, document, video. Any other key, such as viewOnce, is rejected with 400. Videos have no legacy format. A top-level file_url field sends the file as a document, not as a playable video.

The API does not download or check the video when it accepts your request. WhatsApp applies its own limits when the video is delivered: Format Notes MP4 Most compatible format. MOV Apple QuickTime. AVI Windows format. WebM Modern web format.
Format MIME type Extension MP4 video/mp4 .mp4 MOV video/quicktime .mov AVI video/x-msvideo .avi WebM video/webm .webm MKV video/x-matroska .mkv

Maximum file size: 64 MB. Recommended duration: up to 90 seconds for reliable delivery. Accessibility: the URL must be public and point directly to the video file. Processing: WhatsApp may compress the video when it is delivered.

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "file", "params": { "video": { "url": "https://example.com/videos/demo.mp4" }, "mimetype": "video/mp4", "caption": "Check out this amazing video! 🎥✨" } }' In these examples, 6281234567890 is your device (the phone from List devices) and 6289876543210 is the receiver. Replace both with your own numbers.

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "file", "params": { "video": { "url": "https://example.com/videos/product-demo.mp4" }, "mimetype": "video/mp4", "caption": "🎉 *NEW PRODUCT DEMO* 🎉

_Watch our latest innovation in action_

✅ Easy to Use
✅ Powerful Features
✅ Lightning Fast

*Available Now!*

Order today: https://shop.example.com" } }'

curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "6281234567890", "receiver": "6289876543210", "type": "file", "params": { "video": { "url": "https://example.com/videos/tutorial.mp4" }, "mimetype": "video/mp4" } }'

A successful request returns HTTP 200 with the queued message. The fields are the same as for text messages. For a video: type is file. body holds the caption, or an empty string without one. params holds the video URL, MIME type, and caption. file_url, file_name, and file_mime are null. { "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "id": 36259786, "device_id": 12, "from_number": "6281234567890", "to_number": "6289876543210", "type": "file", "msg_type": "outgoing", "body": "Check out this amazing video! 🎥✨", "status": "PENDING", "wa_id": null, "retry": 0, "failed_reason": null, "file_url": null, "file_name": null, "file_caption": null, "file_size": null, "file_mime": null, "params": { "caption": "Check out this amazing video! 🎥✨", "mimetype": "video/mp4", "video": { "url": "https://example.com/videos/demo.mp4" } }, "is_group": false, "created_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z", "updated_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z" } }

In this tutorial you get an API token, connect a WhatsApp number, and send your first message with curl. It takes about 5 minutes.

You need: A Whatspie account. Sign up or log in at app.whatspie.com. A phone with WhatsApp. You scan a QR code with it to connect its number to Whatspie. A terminal with curl. On Windows PowerShell, type curl.exe instead of curl.

In the dashboard, open Developers in the sidebar, or go to app.whatspie.com/profile?tab=developer. Copy your API token. Treat it like a password. In the commands below, replace YOUR_API_TOKEN with it. See Authentication for details.

A device is one WhatsApp number connected to Whatspie. Every message you send goes through a device. In the dashboard, open Devices in the sidebar and click Add Device. Enter a Device Name, for example Test phone. Choose a package. To try Whatspie, choose the Free package (BETA, one per account). Compare Free and Paid features on the pricing page. Click Create Device.

In Devices, click Connect next to your new device. A QR code appears. On your phone, open WhatsApp, go to Linked devices, and tap Link a device. Scan the QR code. You have about 20 seconds; if it expires, click Connect again.

List your devices. This checks your token without sending a message: curl 'https://api.whatspie.com/devices' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' The response looks like this (fields trimmed). data is a list with one entry per device: { "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": [ { "id": 12, "phone": "6281234567890", "paired_status": "PAIRED" } ] } Find your device in data: "paired_status": "PAIRED" means it is connected to WhatsApp. If it says UNPAIRED, repeat Step 3. "phone" is its WhatsApp number. This is YOUR_DEVICE_PHONE in the next step. Use phone, not id: id is only for /devices/{id} URLs. If you get 403 Invalid Authentication Token, copy the token again from Step 1.
documents.s: Step 4: Check your token and device

documents.t: Replace YOUR_API_TOKEN, YOUR_DEVICE_PHONE (from Step 4), and RECEIVER_PHONE (a number you can check on a phone). Write numbers in international format without +, for example 6281234567890 (Indonesia: replace the first 0 with 62). curl -X POST 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -d '{ "device": "YOUR_DEVICE_PHONE", "receiver": "RECEIVER_PHONE", "type": "chat", "params": { "text": "Hi!" } }' A successful request returns the queued message. In this example the device is 6281234567890 and the receiver is 6289876543210: { "status": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "id": 36259782, "device_id": 12, "from_number": "6281234567890", "to_number": "6289876543210", "type": "chat", "msg_type": "outgoing", "body": "Hi!", "status": "PENDING", "wa_id": null, "retry": 0, "failed_reason": null, "file_url": null, "file_name": null, "file_caption": null, "file_size": null, "file_mime": null, "params": { "text": "Hi!" }, "is_group": false, "created_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z", "updated_at": "2025-08-22T03:36:02Z" } } PENDING means the message is queued for sending, not yet delivered. Note data.id for the next step. If the request fails instead: 403 Device not found or access denied: device is not a connected device on your account. Use the phone from Step 4; see Connect your first device. 403 Invalid Authentication Token: the token is wrong. See Authentication.

Open WhatsApp on the receiving phone: the message "Hi!" arrives from your device's number. You can also check it with the API. Replace MESSAGE_ID with data.id from Step 5: curl 'https://api.whatspie.com/messages/MESSAGE_ID' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' data.status changes as delivery progresses: SENT, then RECEIVED, then READ. If it is ERROR, data.failed_reason says why, for example a disconnected device or a number that is not on WhatsApp. See Status values. You have sent your first message with the Whatspie API.
Send images, files, videos, and locations Send messages to groups Receive incoming messages with webhooks Messaging guide: code helpers, batch sending, and retries No code? Use Claude with MCP

Webhooks send events from your WhatsApp device to your application. When your device receives a message, Whatspie sends it to your webhook URL as an HTTP POST with a JSON body. Your endpoint can reply to the message by returning JSON.
https://api.whatspie.com

Set the webhook URL in your device settings: Open device configuration: go to Devices → Configuration in the Whatspie dashboard. Add the webhook URL: enter your endpoint URL. Save the configuration: your endpoint must accept POST requests with a JSON body. When you save, the device connection reloads its configuration, so the new settings apply right away. The device's current webhook_url is shown by Get device.
Every webhook is an HTTP POST with these headers: Header Value Content-Type application/json User-Agent WhatsPie-Webhook/1.0
Use HTTPS. Respond within 10 seconds. Whatspie stops waiting after 10 seconds. Respond with an HTTP 2xx status. Failed deliveries are not retried. If your endpoint is down or slow, the event is lost.

In Device Configuration → Webhook, choose the webhook version: v1 (default): only incoming messages are sent, in the format shown in Incoming message formats. v2: every event uses the envelope { "type": "<event_type>", "data": { ... } }, and you choose which events to receive. See Webhook v2 events.

Incoming messages are sent for personal chats and groups. Messages you send yourself, status updates, and channel (newsletter) posts are not sent. Message type in the payload Packages Text text All Reaction reaction All Contact card contactMessage or contactsArrayMessage All Image imageMessage All except BETA Document documentMessage All except BETA Audio and voice notes audioMessage All except BETA Other message types, such as video, stickers, and locations, are not sent to the webhook. On the BETA package, images, documents, and audio are not sent either.

All incoming messages share these fields: Field Type Description type string Message type; see the table above. from string Sender's phone number. For a group message, the chat the message came from. participant string or null In a group, the member who sent the message. null in personal chats. timestamp integer Unix timestamp of the message. message_id string WhatsApp message ID. Use it as message_id in Send reaction. from_user.name string Sender's WhatsApp display name. from_user.jid string WhatsApp ID of the chat. May be in WhatsApp's newer @lid format instead of a phone number. key object WhatsApp's raw message key. When key.remoteJid is in the @lid format, the sender's number is in key.remoteJidAlt (<number>@s.whatsapp.net). is_forwared boolean Always false. Note the spelling: the field is named is_forwared. is_broadcast boolean Always false. is_group boolean true for a group message. created_at string When Whatspie processed the message, ISO 8601.

With Webhook version set to v2, every request body has: type: the event type. data: the event payload. type Sent when Default message_incoming Your device receives a message. On, unless you turn it off message_sent A message you sent reaches WhatsApp's servers. Off, unless you turn it on message_read The recipient reads a message you sent. Off, unless you turn it on message_failed A message you sent fails. Off, unless you turn it on device_connected The device connects to WhatsApp. Off, unless you turn it on device_disconnected The device session ends, for example logged out or replaced. Not sent for short reconnections. Off, unless you turn it on Turn events on or off in the device webhook settings. In the message events below, message_id is WhatsApp's message ID: the same value as wa_id in Get message, not the numeric Whatspie id.

The same content as a v1 incoming message, wrapped in data: { "type": "message_incoming", "data": { "type": "text", "message": "Hello, I need help with my order", "from": "62856123456", "participant": null, "timestamp": 1581651709, "message_id": "3219EDE2131", "from_user": { "name": "John Doe", "jid": "62856123456@s.whatsapp.net" }, "is_forwared": false, "is_broadcast": false, "is_group": false } }

{ "type": "message_sent", "data": { "message_id": "3EB0C767D26A1D8B12A3", "wa_message_id": "3EB0C767D26A1D8B12A3", "status": "SENT", "sent_at": "2026-02-03T10:00:00.000Z" } } Field Type Description message_id string WhatsApp message ID. wa_message_id string Same value as message_id. status string SENT. sent_at string When the event was sent, ISO 8601.

{ "type": "message_read", "data": { "message_id": "3EB0C767D26A1D8B12A3", "wa_message_id": "3EB0C767D26A1D8B12A3", "read_at": "2026-02-03T10:00:00.000Z" } } Field Type Description message_id string WhatsApp message ID. wa_message_id string Same value as message_id. read_at string When the read receipt arrived, ISO 8601.

{ "type": "message_failed", "data": { "message_id": "3EB0C767D26A1D8B12A3", "status": "ERROR", "reason": "Invalid WhatsApp Number" } } Field Type Description message_id string WhatsApp message ID. status string ERROR. reason string Why the message failed.
{ "type": "device_connected", "data": { "device_id": "2076", "status": "PAIRED", "reason": "Connected" } }

{ "type": "device_disconnected", "data": { "device_id": "2076", "status": "UNPAIRED", "reason": "Conflict" } } Field Type Description device_id string Whatspie device ID, the same as id in Device management. status string PAIRED for connected, UNPAIRED for disconnected. reason string Why the connection changed, for example Conflict or Logged out.

Your endpoint can reply to an incoming message by returning JSON in the response body. Replies work only for incoming messages, not for the other v2 events. If you do not want to reply, return any 2xx response; an empty or non-JSON body sends nothing. Replies go to the chat the message came from, including groups. Each reply counts toward your message quota and is skipped when the quota is used up.

{ "type": "chat", "body": "Thank you for your message! We'll get back to you shortly." } Field Type Required Description type string Yes chat to send a message, reaction to react. body string Yes, without params Reply text. params object No Message content for media replies. When set, params is sent instead of body.

When params is set, only params is sent; body is not sent as a separate message. Put any text in caption: { "type": "chat", "body": "Here's the information you requested:", "params": { "image": { "url": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1653764982079-c7c5e4fd682a" }, "caption": "Product catalog 2024" } }

{ "type": "chat", "body": "Please find the requested document attached:", "params": { "document": { "url": "https://example.com/files/sample.pdf" }, "fileName": "price_list.pdf", "mimetype": "application/pdf" } }
React to the incoming message with an emoji: { "type": "reaction", "body": "👍" }
Return an array to send several replies in order: [ { "type": "chat", "body": "Thank you for your inquiry!" }, { "type": "chat", "body": "Our team will contact you within 24 hours." } ]

These message types are deprecated and should not be used in new integrations: Button messages: use regular text messages instead. Template messages: use regular text with images instead. List messages: use regular text with structured formatting instead.

Verify the origin: Whatspie does not sign webhook requests. Use a long, hard-to-guess URL, for example with a secret token in the path, and reject requests to other paths. Use HTTPS: always use TLS for your endpoint. Validate input: treat every field as untrusted data.
Quick response: respond within 10 seconds. Async processing: put slow work in a queue and respond right away. Status codes: return 2xx once you have accepted the event.

Duplicate detection: use message_id to avoid processing the same message twice. Message types: handle every type you may receive, and ignore the rest. Fallback responses: decide what to do with messages you cannot handle.

A basic webhook handler in Node.js with Express: const express = require('express'); const app = express(); app.use(express.json()); app.post('/webhook', (req, res) => { // v2 wraps every event; v1 sends the incoming message directly const event = req.body.type && req.body.data ? req.body : { type: 'message_incoming', data: req.body }; if (event.type !== 'message_incoming') { console.log('Event:', event.type, event.data); return res.sendStatus(200); // no reply for non-message events } const message = event.data; if (message.type === 'documentMessage') { return res.json({ type: 'chat', body: "Thank you for the document. We'll review it shortly.", }); } if (message.type === 'text') { return res.json({ type: 'chat', body: processTextMessage(message.message), }); } res.json({ type: 'chat', body: 'Message received successfully!', }); }); function processTextMessage(text) { if (text.toLowerCase().includes('help')) { return 'How can I assist you today?'; } return 'Thanks for your message!'; } app.listen(3000, () => { console.log('Webhook server running on port 3000'); });

Check that the webhook URL is set in the device configuration. Check that your endpoint is reachable from the internet over HTTPS. Check that the device is connected (paired_status is PAIRED). Check the message type: video, stickers, and locations are not sent, and files are not sent on the BETA package.
Return a JSON body with type set to chat or reaction. Respond within 10 seconds. Check that your message quota is not used up. Check that the device is connected and active.
File URLs expire after 24 hours. Download files as soon as you receive them. Handle failed downloads and retry them. Consider a queue for reliable file processing.
